entries.lead: the siege of breda of 1624–1625 occurred during the eighty years' war and was carried out by the army of flanders.

entries.label: Siege of Breda (1637)
entries.lead: the fourth siege of breda was an important siege in the eighty years' war in which stadtholder frederick henry, prince of orange retook the city of breda, which had last changed hands in 1625 when the spanish general ambrogio spinola conquered it for the spanish habsburgs.

entries.label: Siege of Breisach
entries.lead: the siege of breisach was fought on 18 august — 17 december 1638 as part of the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Brescia (1438–1440)
entries.lead: the siege of brescia in 1438–1440 was an attempt by the duchy of milan to capture the city of brescia, annexed in 1428 by the republic of venice, during the wars in lombardy.

entries.label: Siege of Brieg
entries.lead: the siege of brieg or siege of brzeg resulted in the surrender of the habsburg austrian garrison of brzeg (brieg) during the war of the austrian succession.

entries.label: Siege of Brimstone Hill
entries.lead: the french invasion of saint kitts also known as the siege of brimstone hill, from 19 january–13 february 1782, was a part of the american revolutionary war.

entries.label: Siege of Brno
entries.lead: the siege of brno, which occurred from 3 may to 23 august 1645, was the second swedish siege of the city of brno in the last years of the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Brussels
entries.lead: the siege of brussels took place between january and february 1746 during the war of the austrian succession.

entries.label: Siege of Buda (1529)
entries.lead: the siege of buda was a military operation led by the ottoman empire with the aim of capturing buda and installing john zapolya as its ruler.

entries.label: Siege of Buda (1541)
entries.lead: the siege of buda ended with the capture of the city of buda, the historical capital of the kingdom of hungary, by the ottoman empire, leading to about 150 years of ottoman rule in parts of hungary.

entries.label: Siege of Buda (1684)
entries.lead: the siege of buda was a siege by the holy roman empire of the ottoman fortress of buda.

entries.label: Siege of Buda (1686)
entries.lead: the siege of buda was a military engagement during the great turkish war, in which forces of the holy league, led by the habsburg monarchy, recaptured the fortified city of buda from the ottoman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Buda (1849)
entries.lead: the siege of buda took place at buda castle, part of the twin capital cities of the kingdom of hungary.

entries.label: Siege of Burgos
entries.lead: at the siege of burgos, from 19 september to 21 october 1812, the anglo-portuguese army led by general arthur wellesley, marquess of wellington tried to capture the castle of burgos from its french garrison under the command of general of brigade jean-louis dubreton.

entries.label: Siege of Busanjin
entries.lead: the siege of busanjin was a battle fought at busan on 24 may 1592, between japanese and korean forces.

entries.label: Siege of Butrint (1798)
entries.lead: the siege of butrint took place on 18–25 october [o.s.

entries.label: Siege of Caçapava
entries.lead: the siege of cacapava was a military victory by the rebel forces during the ragamuffin war in april 1837.

entries.label: Siege of Cádiz
entries.lead: the french army besieged the large spanish naval base of cadiz from 5 february 1810 to 24 august 1812 during the peninsular war.

entries.label: Siege of Cairo (1801)
entries.lead: the siege of cairo, also known as the cairo campaign, took place during the french invasion of egypt and syria.

entries.label: Siege of Calais (1558)
entries.lead: the french siege of calais in early 1558 was part of the italian war of 1551–1559 between france and england and their respective allies.

entries.label: Siege of Calcutta
entries.lead: the siege of calcutta was a battle between the bengal subah and the british east india company on 20 june 1756.

entries.label: Siege of Cambrai (1677)
entries.lead: the siege of cambrai took place from 20 march to 19 april 1677 during the 1672–1678 franco-dutch war; then part of the spanish netherlands, it was invested by a french army under the duc de luxembourg.

entries.label: Siege of Campar
entries.lead: the siege of campar was a 1543 military conflict between the kingdom of portugal and the combined forces of mahmud and the sultanates of bintang and lingga.

entries.label: Siege of Candia
entries.lead: in the siege of candia, ottoman forces besieged the venetian-ruled capital city of the kingdom of candia.

entries.label: Siege of Cannanore (1507)
entries.lead: the siege of cannanore was a four-month siege, from 27 april 1507 to 27 august 1507, when troops of the local ruler, supported by the zamorin of calicut besieged the portuguese garrison at st.

entries.label: Siege of Capua (1734)
entries.lead: the siege of capua was the last major military action of the war of the polish succession in the kingdom of naples.

entries.label: Siege of Cassel (1761)
entries.lead: the siege of cassel was a failed attempt by duke ferdinand of brunswick to capture french-held kassel, the capital of hesse-kassel.

entries.label: Siege of Castelnuovo
entries.lead: the siege of castelnuovo was an engagement during the ottoman-habsburg struggle for control of the mediterranean, which took place in july 1539 at the walled town of castelnuovo, present-day herceg novi, montenegro.

entries.label: Siege of Catubig
entries.lead: the siege of catubig was a long and bloody engagement fought during the philippine–american war, in which filipino guerrillas launched a surprise attack against a detachment of u.s.

entries.label: Siege of Cawnpore
entries.lead: the siege of cawnpore was a key episode in the indian rebellion of 1857.

entries.label: Siege of Ceuta (1419)
entries.lead: the siege of ceuta of 1419 was fought between the besieging forces of the marinid sultanate, led by sultan abu said uthman iii, including allied forces from the emirate of granada, and the portuguese garrison of ceuta, led by pedro de menezes, 1st count of vila real.

entries.label: Siege of Ceuta (1790–1791)
entries.lead: the siege of ceuta (1790–1791) was an armed confrontation between the kingdom of spain and the sultanate of morocco during the spanish-moroccan war of 1790–1791.

entries.label: Siege of Charleston
entries.lead: the siege of charleston was a major engagement and major british victory in the american revolutionary war, fought in the environs of charles town, between march 29 and may 12, 1780.

entries.label: Siege of Chaul (1570–1571)
entries.lead: the siege of chaul was a military operation undertaken by the ahmadnagar sultanate against the portuguese city of chaul in the maharashtra, india, between december 1570 and july 1571.

entries.label: Siege of Chittorgarh (1567–1568)
entries.lead: the siege of chittorgarh was the military expedition of the mughal empire under akbar against the kingdom of mewar that commenced in 1567 during which the mughals successfully captured the fort of chittorgarh after a hard-pressed siege which lasted for several months.

entries.label: Siege of Chōkō-ji
entries.lead: choko-ji (長興寺) was a temple captured by oda nobunaga from the rokkaku clan in 1568.

entries.label: Siege of Ciudad Rodrigo (1810)
entries.lead: in the siege of ciudad rodrigo, in salamanca, spain, the french marshal michel ney took the fortified city from field marshal andres perez de herrasti on 10 july 1810 after a siege that began on 26 april.

entries.label: Siege of Ciudad Rodrigo (1812)
entries.lead: the siege of ciudad rodrigo was the successful investment of the french-occupied city of ciudad rodrigo by lord wellington's anglo-portuguese army from 7–20 january 1812.

entries.label: Siege of Colombo (1587–1588)
entries.lead: the siege of colombo from 1587 to 1588 was a military conflict between the portuguese and the sinhalese troops of the king of sitawaka over control of colombo, on the island of ceylon, now sri lanka.

entries.label: Siege of Colonia del Sacramento
entries.lead: the siege of colonia del sacramento was a successful siege in 1704 by spanish forces of the portuguese colonial town of colonia del sacramento, opposite buenos aires and now in the nation of uruguay.

entries.label: Siege of Compiègne
entries.lead: the siege of compiegne (1430) was conducted by duke philip iii of burgundy after the town of compiegne had refused to transfer allegiance to him under the terms of a treaty with charles vii of france.

entries.label: Siege of Concepción
entries.lead: during the siege of concepcion of the arauco war, 20,000 warriors of the army of the mapuche laid siege to the spanish garrison and civil population in the fortress of concepcion, chile.

entries.label: Siege of Constantine
entries.lead: the siege of constantine was a blockade and assault on constantine in october 1837 by french forces during the french conquest of algeria.

entries.label: Siege of Constantinople (1422)
entries.lead: in 1422, the ottoman empire laid siege to constantinople, the capital of the byzantine empire, as a result of the byzantine emperor manuel ii's attempts to interfere in the succession of ottoman sultans, after the death of mehmed i in 1421.

entries.label: Siege of Corfu (1537)
entries.lead: the siege of corfu in 1537 was led by the ottoman emperor suleiman the magnificent, against the republic of venice-held island of corfu.

entries.label: Siege of Corfu (1716)
entries.lead: the siege of corfu took place on 8 july – 21 august 1716, when the ottoman empire besieged the city of corfu, on the namesake island, then held by the republic of venice.

entries.label: Siege of Corfu (1798–1799)
entries.lead: the siege of corfu was a military operation by a joint russian and turkish fleet against french troops occupying the fortified island of corfu; ended in coalition victory.

entries.label: Siege of Corinth
entries.lead: the siege of corinth, also known as the first battle of corinth, was an american civil war engagement lasting from april 29 to may 30, 1862, in corinth, mississippi.

entries.label: Siege of Coron (1533–1534)
entries.lead: the siege of coron in 1533–1534 was a two-part attempt by the ottoman empire the recapture of the fortress of koroni (coron) in messenia, greece, by the ottoman empire, after the fortress was occupied by emperor charles v's army in 1532.

entries.label: Siege of Crema (1514)
entries.lead: the siege of crema in 1514 was a significant military engagement set within the broader context of political and martial upheaval in early 16th-century italy, particularly during the war of the league of cambrai.

entries.label: Siege of Cuautla
entries.lead: the siege of cuautla was a battle of the war of mexican independence that occurred from 19 february through 2 may 1812 at cuautla, morelos.

entries.label: Siege of Cuddalore
entries.lead: the siege of cuddalore was a siege attempt by british troops against a combined french and mysorean garrison at the fortress of cuddalore in the second anglo-mysore war.

entries.label: Siege of Cuddalore (1748)
entries.lead: the siege of cuddalore was a battle during the war of the austrian succession on 17 june 1748.

entries.label: Siege of Cuneo (1691)
entries.lead: the siege of cuneo was fought on 28 june 1691 during the nine years' war in piedmont-savoy, modern-day northern italy.

entries.label: Siege of Cusco
entries.lead: the 10-month siege of cusco by the incan army under the command of sapa inca manco inca yupanqui started on 6 may 1536 and ended in march 1537.

entries.label: Siege of Cusco (1781)
entries.lead: the siege of cusco, also known as the battle of cusco, was one of the most decisive engagements during the first phase of the rebellion of tupac amaru ii.

entries.label: Siege of Danzig (1734)
entries.lead: the siege of danzig of 1734 was the russian encirclement and capture of the polish city-port of gdansk, during the war of polish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Danzig (1807)
entries.lead: the siege of danzig was the french encirclement and capture of danzig during the war of the fourth coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Danzig (1813)
entries.lead: the siege of danzig was a siege of the city of danzig during the war of the sixth coalition by russian and prussian forces against jean rapp's permanent french garrison, which had been augmented by soldiers from the grande armee retreating from its russian campaign.

entries.label: Siege of Darwar
entries.lead: the siege of darwar was a 29 week siege of the fort at dharwad in 1790 and 1791, then near the frontier, between the kingdom of mysore and the maratha empire.

entries.label: Siege of Delhi (1804)
entries.lead: the siege of delhi was conducted by the maratha leader maharaja yashwantrao holkar against the forces of the british east india company, who were assisting the mughals in defending delhi during the second anglo-maratha war.

entries.label: Siege of Delhi (1857)
entries.lead: the siege of delhi was a decisive conflict of the indian rebellion of 1857.

entries.label: Siege of Demmin
entries.lead: the siege of demnin was a swedish siege of the pomeranian town of demmin during the thirty years' war, the siege would result in a swedish victory.

entries.label: Siege of Derry
entries.lead: the siege of derry in 1689 was the first major event in the williamite war in ireland.

entries.label: Siege of Detroit
entries.lead: the siege of detroit, also known as the surrender of detroit or the battle of fort detroit, was an early engagement in the war of 1812.

entries.label: Siege of Deventer (1578)
entries.lead: the siege of deventer was a siege of the city of deventer by states troops under george van lalaing, count of rennenberg, from 3 august to 19 november 1578 during the eighty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Deventer (1591)
entries.lead: the siege of deventer was a siege of the city of deventer from 1 to 10 june 1591 during the eighty years' war by dutch and english troops under maurice of nassau in an attempt to retake it from its spanish garrison, commanded by herman van den bergh on behalf of the spanish.

entries.label: Siege of Dijon
entries.lead: the siege of dijon between 8 and 13 september 1513 was a successful campaign of the swiss army against the french city of dijon during the war of the league of cambrai.

entries.label: Siege of Dimdim
entries.lead: the siege of dimdim was an operation orchestrated by the safavid ruler shah abbas i, in which his forces besieged the dimdim castle of the rebellious kurdish emirate of bradost from november 1609 to the summer of 1610.

entries.label: Siege of Diriyah
entries.lead: the siege of diriyah was a successful ottoman siege that took place in late 1818 at the end of the wahhabi war of 1811–1818 during the nejd expedition.

entries.label: Siege of Diu (1531)
entries.lead: the siege of diu occurred when a combined ottoman-gujarati force defeated a portuguese attempt to capture the city of diu in 1531.

entries.label: Siege of Diu (1538)
entries.lead: the siege of diu occurred when an army of the sultanate of gujarat under khadjar safar, aided by forces of the ottoman empire, attempted to capture the city of diu in 1538, then held by the portuguese.

entries.label: Siege of Diu (1546)
entries.lead: the 1546 siege of diu, also known as the second siege of diu was conducted by joint forces of the ottoman empire and gujarat sultanate against the portuguese indian city of diu.

entries.label: Siege of Dongnae
entries.lead: the siege of dongnae was a siege that occurred on may 25, 1592 during the 1592–1598 japanese invasions of korea.

entries.label: Siege of Dorsten
entries.lead: in the siege of dorsten, an imperial force under melchior von hatzfeldt besieged the hessian garrison in the town of dorsten from 16 july 1641 to 19 september 1641 during the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Doullens
entries.lead: the siege of doullens, also known as the spanish capture of doullens or the storming of doullens, took place between 14 and 31 july 1595, as part of the franco-spanish war (1595–1598), in the context of the french wars of religion.

entries.label: Siege of Dresden
entries.lead: the siege of dresden took place in july 1760 during the third silesian war when a prussian force led by frederick the great unsuccessfully besieged the city of dresden in saxony.

entries.label: Siege of Drogheda
entries.lead: the siege of drogheda, 3 to 11 september 1649, took place at the start of the cromwellian conquest of ireland.

entries.label: Siege of Dunboy
entries.lead: the siege of dunboy took place at dunboy castle between 5 june and 18 june 1602, during the nine years' war in ireland.

entries.label: Siege of Dunkirk (1646)
entries.lead: the siege of dunkirk was a siege commenced by france under the command of louis, le grand conde with naval support of the dutch republic under the command of admiral maarten tromp, who were able to blockade the city to help conde's siege.

entries.label: Siege of Dunlap's Station
entries.lead: the siege of dunlap's station was a battle that took place on january 10–11, 1791, during the northwest indian war between the northwestern confederacy of american indians and european american settlers in what became the southwestern region of the u.s.

entries.label: Siege of Edo
entries.lead: in the 1524 siege of edo, also known as the battle of takanawahara (高輪原の戦い), the hojo, led by hojo ujitsuna, besieged edo castle, which was held by uesugi tomooki.

entries.label: Siege of Eger (1552)
entries.lead: the siege of eger occurred during the 16th century ottoman wars in europe.

entries.label: Siege of Eger (1596)
entries.lead: the ottomans laid siege to the city of eger, that lasted from september 20 to october 12, 1596, as part of the long war, successfully conquering it after the 7,000 defenders of the fortress, mostly foreign mercenaries, were killed by the ottoman forces commanded by the sultan mehmed iii himself, who

entries.label: Siege of Eger (1647)
entries.lead: the siege of eger was conducted by the swedish army under carl gustaf wrangel.

entries.label: Siege of El Arish
entries.lead: the siege of el arish was a successful siege by french forces under napoleon bonaparte against ottoman forces under mustafa pasha.

entries.label: Siege of El Rahmaniya
entries.lead: the siege of el rahmaniya was initiated by an anglo-ottoman force against the french troops in el rahmaniya.

entries.label: Siege of Erivan (1635)
entries.lead: the siege of erivan was a military engagement of the ottoman–safavid war (1623–1639).

entries.label: Siege of Erivan (1804)
entries.lead: the siege of erivan took place from july to september 1804, during the russo-persian war (1804–1813).

entries.label: Siege of Érsekújvár (1685)
entries.lead: the siege of ersekujvar was fought between july 7 and august 17 of 1685, between the besieging habsburg army and the ottoman garrison of ersekujvar, city in what is today nove zamky, slovakia .

entries.label: Siege of Eshowe
entries.lead: the siege of eshowe took place during the anglo-zulu war of 1879.

entries.label: Siege of Esztergom (1543)
entries.lead: the siege of esztergom occurred between 25 july and 10 august 1543, when the ottoman army, led by sultan suleiman the magnificent, besieged the city of esztergom in modern hungary.

entries.label: Siege of Famagusta
entries.lead: the siege of famagusta happened in venetian-controlled famagusta, the last christian possession in cyprus.

entries.label: Siege of Fellin
entries.lead: the siege of fellin took place between 25 march and 17 may 1602 during the polish–swedish war (1600–1611).

entries.label: Siege of Figueras (1811)
entries.lead: the siege of figueras, which lasted from 10 april to 19 august 1811, saw the spanish garrison of sant ferran castle led by brigadier general juan antonio martinez defend against an imperial french force commanded by marshal jacques macdonald and his deputy louis baraguey d'hilliers.

entries.label: Siege of Florence (1529–1530)
entries.lead: the siege of florence took place from 24 october 1529 to 10 august 1530, at the end of the war of the league of cognac.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Detroit
entries.lead: the siege of fort detroit was an ultimately unsuccessful attempt by north american natives to capture fort detroit during pontiac's war.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Erie
entries.lead: the siege of fort erie, also known as the battle of erie, from 4 august to 21 september 1814, was one of the last engagements of the war of 1812, between british and american forces.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Julien
entries.lead: the siege of fort julien was a military engagement that took place during the french revolutionary wars as part of the french invasion of egypt and syria from 8 to 19 april 1801.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Mackinac
entries.lead: the capture of fort mackinac was one of the first engagements of the war of 1812.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Macon
entries.lead: the siege of fort macon took place from march 23 to april 26, 1862, on the outer banks of carteret county, north carolina.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Massachusetts
entries.lead: the siege of fort massachusetts was a successful siege of fort massachusetts by a mixed force of more than 1,000 french and native americans from new france.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Meigs
entries.lead: the siege of fort meigs was a significant war of 1812 military engagement in northwestern ohio during the spring of 1813.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Mifflin
entries.lead: the siege of fort mifflin or the siege of mud island fort, which took place from september 26 to november 16, 1777, saw british land batteries commanded by captain john montresor and a british naval squadron under vice admiral lord richard howe attempt to capture an american fort in the delaware riv

entries.label: Siege of Fort Nashwaak
entries.lead: the siege of fort nashwaak occurred during king william's war when new england forces from boston attacked the capital of acadia, fort nashwaak, at present-day fredericton, new brunswick.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Pilar
entries.lead: the siege of fort pilar was fought between april and may 1898 on then-town of zamboanga in mindanao as a part of the philippine revolution.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Pitt
entries.lead: the siege of fort pitt took place during june and july 1763 in what is now the city of pittsburgh, pennsylvania, united states.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Pulaski
entries.lead: the siege of fort pulaski concluded with the battle of fort pulaski fought april 10–11, 1862, during the american civil war.

entries.label: Siege of Fort St. Jean
entries.lead: the siege of fort st.

entries.label: Siege of Fort St Philip (1756)
entries.lead: the siege of fort st philip, also known as the siege of minorca, took place from 20 april to 29 june 1756 during the seven years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Stanwix
entries.lead: the siege of fort stanwix began on august 2, 1777, and ended on august 22, 1777.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Texas
entries.lead: the siege of fort texas marked the beginning of active campaigning by the armies of the united states and mexico during the mexican–american war.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Ticonderoga (1777)
entries.lead: the siege of fort ticonderoga occurred between 2 july and 6 july 1777 at fort ticonderoga, near the southern end of lake champlain in the state of new york.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Wayne
entries.lead: the siege of fort wayne took place from september 5–12, 1812, during the war of 1812.

entries.label: Siege of Fort William Henry
entries.lead: the siege of fort william henry was conducted by a french and indian force led by louis-joseph de montcalm against the british-held fort william henry.

entries.label: Siege of Fort Zeelandia
entries.lead: the siege of fort zeelandia of 1661–1662 ended the dutch east india company's rule over taiwan and began the kingdom of tungning's rule over the island.

entries.label: Siege of Frankenthal
entries.lead: the siege of frankenthal was a siege of the palatinate campaign during the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Fredriksten
entries.lead: the siege of fredriksten was an attack on the norwegian fortress of fredriksten in the city of fredrikshald by king charles xii of sweden.

entries.label: Siege of Fuenterrabía (1523–1524)
entries.lead: the siege of fuenterrabia took place in 1523-24 by a spanish army, after a franco-navarrese army had taken it in 1521 in a new incursion to reconquer the kingdom of navarre, which had been occupied since 1512 by troops from the unified crown of castile and crown of aragon.

entries.label: Siege of Fuenterrabía (1638)
entries.lead: the siege of hondarribia of 1638 took place in june – september 1638, between spain and france during the thirty years' war and the franco-spanish war (1635-1659).

entries.label: Siege of Fukashi
entries.lead: the 1550 siege of fukashi was one of a series of battles waged by takeda shingen in his long campaign to conquer shinano province, which was ruled by a number of minor daimyo, notably the suwa, ogasawara, murakami and takato.

entries.label: Siege of Fukazawa
entries.lead: the 1571 siege of fukazawa castle was one of a number of battles which formed takeda shingen's campaigns against the hojo clan, during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Fukuyo
entries.lead: the siege of fukuyo was one of many steps taken by the japanese feudal lord takeda shingen in his bid to seize control of shinano province.

entries.label: Siege of Fushimi Castle
entries.lead: the siege of fushimi was a crucial battle in the series leading up to the decisive battle of sekigahara which ended japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Futamata
entries.lead: futamata fortress was takeda shingen's first objective in his campaign against tokugawa ieyasu.

entries.label: Siege of Gaeta (1707)
entries.lead: the siege of gaeta was a three-month siege of the italian city of gaeta in 1707 by the forces of the austrian monarchy under wirich philipp von daun, during the war of the spanish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Gaeta (1734)
entries.lead: the siege of gaeta was a siege during the war of polish succession fought at gaeta, italy.

entries.label: Siege of Gaeta (1806)
entries.lead: the siege of gaeta saw the fortress city of gaeta and its neapolitan garrison under general louis of hesse-philippsthal besieged by an imperial french corps led by marshal andre massena.

entries.label: Siege of Gaeta (1860–1861)
entries.lead: the siege of gaeta was the concluding event of the war between the kingdom of sardinia and the kingdom of the two sicilies, part of the unification of italy.

entries.label: Siege of Galle (1640)
entries.lead: the siege of the portuguese fort santa cruz de gale at galle in 1640, took place during the dutch–portuguese and sinhalese–portuguese wars.

entries.label: Siege of Ganja (1734–1735)
entries.lead: the siege of ganja, during the last phase of the ottoman–persian war (1730–1735), resulted in the surrender of the city by its ottoman garrison after the main turkish army marching to its relief was decisively defeated at the battle of baghavard.

entries.label: Siege of Ganja (1804)
entries.lead: the siege of ganja or assault on ganja or storming of ganja was the result of a russian offensive in the south caucasus intended to conquer the ganja khanate of qajar iran, which contributed to the escalation of the russo-persian war (1804–1813).

entries.label: Siege of Geertruidenberg (1593)
entries.lead: the siege of geertruidenberg was a siege of the city of geertruidenberg that took place between 27 march and 24 june 1593 during the eighty years' war and the anglo–spanish war.

entries.label: Siege of Genoa (1522)
entries.lead: the siege of genoa (1522) took place in may 1522 as part of a larger conflict known as the italian war of 1521–1526.

entries.label: Siege of Genoa (1747)
entries.lead: the siege of genoa took place in 1747 when an austrian army under the command of count schulenburg-oeynhausen launched a failed attempt to capture the capital of the republic of genoa.

entries.label: Siege of Genoa (1800)
entries.lead: the siege of genoa saw an austrian army led by michael von melas besiege the port of genoa, which was occupied by a french garrison under the command of andre massena, from 19 april to 4 june 1800.

entries.label: Siege of Glatz
entries.lead: the siege of glatz took place in 1760 during the third silesian war when an austrian force led by general von laudon laid siege to and successfully stormed the fortress of glatz from its prussian garrison.

entries.label: Siege of Goa (1570–1571)
entries.lead: the siege of goa in 1570–1571 was a major military conflict between the portuguese empire and the sultanate of bijapur, as part of an alliance of asian powers led by ali adil shah i.

entries.label: Siege of Godesberg
entries.lead: the siege of godesberg, 18 november – 17 december 1583, was the first major siege of the cologne war (1583–1589).

entries.label: Siege of Golconda
entries.lead: the siege of golconda (1687) was an eight-month military siege of the golconda fort.

entries.label: Siege of Golubac
entries.lead: the siege of golubac was a military conflict between the hungarian–wallachian–lithuanian alliance and the ottoman empire in may 1428.

entries.label: Siege of Goorumconda
entries.lead: the siege of goorumconda was a series of conflicts fought at goorumconda, a hill fort northeast of bangalore, during the third anglo-mysore war.

entries.label: Siege of Graciosa (1489)
entries.lead: the siege of graciosa was a military campaign launched in 1489 by the wattassid sultan mohammed al-wattasi in order to take the portuguese stronghold of graciosa.

entries.label: Siege of Groenlo (1595)
entries.lead: the siege of grol or groenlo in 1595 was a siege of groenlo by states forces under maurice of nassau during the eighty years' war in an attempt to capture it from the spanish empire.

entries.label: Siege of Groenlo (1606)
entries.lead: the siege of groenlo was a siege of groenlo or grol in 1606 during the dutch revolt.

entries.label: Siege of Groenlo (1627)
entries.lead: the siege of grol in 1627 was a battle between the army of the dutch republic, commanded by frederick henry, prince of orange, and the spanish-controlled fortified city of grol, during the eighty years war and the anglo–spanish war in 1627.

entries.label: Siege of Groningen (1594)
entries.lead: the siege of groningen was a two-month siege which commenced on 19 may 1594, and which took place during the eighty years' war and the anglo-spanish war.

entries.label: Siege of Groningen (1672)
entries.lead: the siege of groningen was a battle that took place in 1672 during the franco-dutch war.

entries.label: Siege of Guadeloupe
entries.lead: the siege of guadeloupe took place from march to may 1703 during the war of the spanish succession, when an english expeditionary force led by christopher codrington landed on guadeloupe in the french west indies, and laid siege to the capital of basse-terre.

entries.label: Siege of Guilin (1647)
entries.lead: the 1647 siege of guilin was a military conflict during the ming-qing transition between the forces of the southern ming dynasty, with the support of a portuguese contingent from macau, against the manchu qing forces.

entries.label: Siege of Gvozdansko
entries.lead: the siege of gvozdansko was an ottoman siege of the fort of gvozdansko in the kingdom of croatia in 1577–1578.

entries.label: Siege of Haarlem
entries.lead: the siege of haarlem was an episode of the eighty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Hachigata (1590)
entries.lead: the 1590 siege of hachigata was the penultimate battle of toyotomi hideyoshi's campaigns against the hojo clan, during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Hamburg
entries.lead: the siege of hamburg took place from december 1813 to may 1814, at the end of the wars of the war of the sixth coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Hammershus
entries.lead: the siege of hammershus occurred from 16 to 17 june 1645 during the torstenson war between sweden and denmark–norway.

entries.label: Siege of Hanazawa
entries.lead: the 1570 siege of hanazawa was one of several battles fought between the takeda and imagawa clans during the takeda's campaign to seize suruga province, during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Harfleur
entries.lead: the siege of harfleur was conducted by the english army of king henry v in normandy, france, during the hundred years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Harput (1516)
entries.lead: 1516 siege"

entries.label: Siege of Hasedō
entries.lead: the siege of hasedo (長谷堂城の戦い) was one of a series of battles fought in the far north of japan's main island of honshu contemporaneous with the famous and decisive campaigns between tokugawa ieyasu and ishida mitsunari further south.

entries.label: Siege of Havana
entries.lead: the siege of havana was the capture of the spanish-held city of havana, cuba in 1762 as part of the war between britain and spain which formed part of the larger seven years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Herat (1448)
entries.lead: ulugh beg and his son abdal-latif mirza marched towards herat in the spring of 1448 in order to take khurasan from his nephew, ala al-dawla mirza, who had escaped to quchan after the defeat at the battle of tarnab.

entries.label: Siege of Hergigo
entries.lead: the siege of hergigo was the failed siege launched by emperor sarsa dengel on the fortified ottoman-held port town of hergigo, mentioned in the imperial chronicle under its saho name of dakhano, located on the coast of the red sea facing the island of massawa, in 1589.

entries.label: Siege of Hijiyama
entries.lead: the 1581 siege of hijiyama was one of the crucial battles in oda nobunaga's campaigns to seize iga province during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Hikida Castle
entries.lead: the 1573 siege of hikida castle was one of many battles the warlord oda nobunaga fought against the azai and asakura clans during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Hlukhiv
entries.lead: the siege of hlukhiv was a battle of the muscovite–polish war (1654–1667).

entries.label: Siege of Huajuapan de León
entries.lead: the siege of huajuapan de leon was a battle of the mexican war of independence that was fought from 5 april to 23 july 1812 at huajuapan de leon, in the mexican state of oaxaca.

entries.label: Siege of Hulst (1596)
entries.lead: the siege of hulst of 1596 took place between mid-july and august 18, 1596, at the city of hulst, province of zeeland, low countries, during the eighty years' war, the anglo-spanish war (1585–1604).

entries.label: Siege of Hulst (1645)
entries.lead: the siege of hulst (1645) was the last major siege of the eighty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Ichijōdani Castle
entries.lead: the 1573 siege of ichijodani castle was undertaken by oda nobunaga, a powerful warlord (daimyo) of japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Inabayama Castle
entries.lead: the siege of inabayama castle of 1567 was the final battle in oda nobunaga's campaign to defeat the saito clan in their mountaintop castle and conquer mino province, japan.

entries.label: Siege of Isfahan
entries.lead: the siege of isfahan was a six-month-long siege of isfahan, the capital of the safavid dynasty of iran, by the hotaki-led afghan army.

entries.label: Siege of Itami (1579)
entries.lead: the second siege of itami castle (伊丹城の戦い), also called the siege of arioka castle (有岡城の戦い) during the sengoku period of japanese history, occurred in 1579, five years after it was seized by oda nobunaga in siege of itami (1574) from the itami clan, and entrusted the castle to araki murashige.

entries.label: Siege of Iwamura Castle
entries.lead: the siege of iwamura was a military event which occurred in 1572 in japan, concurrent with takeda shingen's push into totomi province and the battle of mikatagahara.

entries.label: Siege of Iwaya Castle
entries.lead: the siege of iwaya castle (岩屋城の戦い) was fought in the year 1585 when an army of the shimazu clan put the castle of iwaya, which belonged to the takahashi clan who were vassals of the otomo clan, under siege.

entries.label: Siege of Izmail
entries.lead: the siege of izmail, also called the storming of izmail, was a military action fought in 1790 on the danube near the black sea during the russo-turkish war (1787–1792) and simultaneously the austro-turkish war (1788–1791).

entries.label: Siege of Jacmel
entries.lead: the siege of jacmel was a four-and-half month long siege that took place during the war of the south, a sub-war of the haitian revolution.

entries.label: Siege of Jadotville
entries.lead: the siege of jadotville was a major battle during the congo crisis, that began on 13 september 1961 and lasted for five days.

entries.label: Siege of Jaffa
entries.lead: the siege of jaffa was a military engagement between the french army under napoleon bonaparte and ottoman forces under ahmed al-jazzar.

entries.label: Siege of Jajce (1463)
entries.lead: the siege of jajce was a siege of the town of jajce and its citadel in 1463, in a push by ottomans to conquer as much of the bosnian kingdom, and continuation of the ottoman–hungarian wars.

entries.label: Siege of Janjira
entries.lead: the siege of janjira was a military campaign undertaken by the maratha confederacy, commanded by sambhaji, the second maratha ruler, against the siddis of janjira in january 1682.

entries.label: Siege of Jasna Góra
entries.lead: the siege of jasna gora took place in the winter of 1655 during the second northern war, or 'the deluge' – as the swedish invasion of the polish–lithuanian commonwealth is known.

entries.label: Siege of Jeddah
entries.lead: the siege of jeddah was a naval battle that took place in the harbor of jeddah between a portuguese expeditionary force under lopo soares de albergaria and ottoman elements under selman reis, and egyptian mamluks fleet.

entries.label: Siege of Jerusalem (1834)
entries.lead: the siege of jerusalem of 1834 took place during the peasants' revolt in palestine, which erupted following the entry of egyptian general ibrahim pasha into ottoman syria and his subsequent military conscription demand upon the arab villagers of the region.

entries.label: Siege of Jhansi
entries.lead: the siege of jhansi was a military siege during the indian rebellion of 1857 set on the city of jhansi, uttar pradesh by british forces of the east india company between 24 march and 5 april 1858.

entries.label: Siege of Jinji
entries.lead: the siege of jinji (1690–1698) was a protracted conflict between the mughal empire and the maratha kingdom, wherein the triple-hill fortress of jinji was besieged by a large mughal force in order to capture the embedded maratha king rajaram i.

entries.label: Siege of Jinju (1592)
entries.lead: the first siege of jinju was one of the major land battles during the imjin war – the first occurred during the fall of 1592, and the second one in spring of 1593.

entries.label: Siege of Jinju (1593)
entries.lead: the second siege of jinju was a battle fought on 1593 at jinju fortress during the imjin war.

entries.label: Siege of Johor (1587)
entries.lead: the siege of johor of 1587 was a military operation in which portuguese forces successfully sieged, sacked, and razed johor, capital of its eponymous sultanate.

entries.label: Siege of Jülich (1621–1622)
entries.lead: the siege of julich was a major operation in the second phase of the eighty years' war that took place from 5 september 1621 to 3 february 1622.

entries.label: Siege of Kabul (1504)
entries.lead: in 1504, babur besieged kabul and took the city from the arghuns under mukim beg arghun, to become the new ruler of kabul and ghazni regions.

entries.label: Siege of Kaganoi
entries.lead: the 1584 siege of kaganoi was one of the final battles fought by toyotomi hideyoshi in his bid to gain the lands and power of oda nobunaga, who died two years earlier.

entries.label: Siege of Kaiserswerth
entries.lead: the siege of kaiserswerth, was a siege of the war of the spanish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Kakegawa
entries.lead: the 1569 siege of kakegawa was one of many battles fought by tokugawa ieyasu campaign at suruga province and totomi province against imagawa clan during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Kamakura (1526)
entries.lead: in the 1526 siege of kamakura, satomi sanetaka led forces of the uesugi clan against the hojo, who had taken edo from the uesugi two years earlier.

entries.label: Siege of Kamenets
entries.lead: the siege of kamieniec podolski was laid by the ottoman empire on august 18, 1672, in the polish fortress of kamieniec podolski.

entries.label: Siege of Kaminogō Castle
entries.lead: the siege of kaminogo castle was a battle in 1562, during the sengoku period of japan.

entries.label: Siege of Kanbara
entries.lead: the 1569 siege of kanbara was one of many sieges undertaken by the takeda clan against the territories of the hojo clan during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Kandahar
entries.lead: the siege of kandahar began when nader shah's afsharid army invaded southern afghanistan to topple the last hotaki stronghold of loy kandahar, which was held by hussain hotaki.

entries.label: Siege of Kandahar (1605–1606)
entries.lead: the siege of kandahar lasted from november 1605 to january 1606 and was led by the persians to capture the mughal frontier city of kandahar.

entries.label: Siege of Kandahar (1648–1649)
entries.lead: the siege of kandahar, also known as the kandahar campaign, was led by shah abbas ii of safavid empire against the mughal-held city of kandahar, in modern-day afghanistan.

entries.label: Siege of Kanegasaki (1570)
entries.lead: the 1570 siege of kanegasaki took place during oda nobunaga's conflict with the asakura clan in echizen province, which was allied with azai nagamasa.

entries.label: Siege of Kanie
entries.lead: the 1584 siege of kanie was one of many elements in toyotomi hideyoshi's campaign to consolidate his power over the lands held by the oda clan in owari province, japan.

entries.label: Siege of Kanizsa (1601)
entries.lead: during the siege of nagykanizsa in 1601, a small ottoman force held the fortress of nagykanizsa in western hungary against a much larger coalition army of the habsburg monarchy, while inflicting heavy losses on its besiegers.

entries.label: Siege of Kannomine
entries.lead: the 1554 siege of kannomine was one of many battles fought in takeda shingen's campaign to seize control of shinano province.

entries.label: Siege of Kars
entries.lead: the siege of kars was the last major operation of the crimean war.

entries.label: Siege of Kars (1744)
entries.lead: the siege of kars took place in 1744 during the ottoman–persian war of 1743–1746.

entries.label: Siege of Katsurao
entries.lead: the 1553 siege of katsurao was one of many sieges undertaken by the warlord takeda shingen in his long campaign to gain control of japan's shinano province, which was ruled by a hodgepodge of minor daimyo, notably the suwa, ogasawara, murakami and takato.

entries.label: Siege of Katsurayama
entries.lead: the siege of katsurayama in march 1557 was fought between the forces of the japanese daimyo takeda shingen and uesugi kenshin as part of the kawanakajima campaigns.

entries.label: Siege of Kawagoe Castle
entries.lead: the 1545–1546 siege of kawagoe castle was part of a failed attempt by the uesugi clan to regain kawagoe castle from the later hojo clan in the sengoku period of japan.

entries.label: Siege of Kayseri (1490)
entries.lead: the 1490 siege of kayseri took place during the ottoman–mamluk war (1485–1491).

entries.label: Siege of Kayseri (1651)
entries.lead: the 1651 siege of kayseri took place during the celali rebellions in central anatolia.

entries.label: Siege of Kazan
entries.lead: the siege of kazan, also known as the fall of kazan, was the decisive military campaign of the russo-kazan wars in 1552 that resulted in the capture of kazan and the annexation of the khanate of kazan by the tsardom of russia.

entries.label: Siege of Kehl (1703)
entries.lead: the 1703 siege of kehl was a military action of the war of the spanish succession, in which french and spanish forces under the command of the duc de villars captured the fortress of the holy roman empire at kehl, opposite strasbourg on the rhine river.

entries.label: Siege of Kehl (1733)
entries.lead: the siege of kehl was one of the opening moves of the french rhineland campaign in the war of the polish succession, at the fortress town of kehl in the upper rhine river valley in the holy roman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Kemah (1515)
entries.lead: 1515 siege of kemah, erzincan by the ottoman empire"

entries.label: Siege of Kerman
entries.lead: the siege of kerman (1794) was the capture of the city of kerman by the qajar forces led by agha mohammad khan qajar against zand forces led by lotf ali khan which resulted in a decisive qajar victory.

entries.label: Siege of Khartoum
entries.lead: the siege of khartoum took place from 13 march 1884 to 26 january 1885.

entries.label: Siege of Khotyn (1788)
entries.lead: the siege of khotyn took place in khotyn, modern-day ukraine, in 2 july–19 september 1788, and was part of the austro-turkish war and the russo-turkish war.

entries.label: Siege of Kimberley
entries.lead: the siege of kimberley took place during the second boer war at kimberley, cape colony, when boer forces from the orange free state and the transvaal besieged the diamond mining town.

entries.label: Siege of Kinsale
entries.lead: the siege of kinsale, also known as the battle of kinsale, was the ultimate battle in england's conquest of gaelic ireland, commencing in october 1601, near the end of the reign of queen elizabeth i, and at the climax of the nine years' war—a campaign by hugh o'neill, hugh roe o'donnell and other ir

entries.label: Siege of Kiso Fukushima
entries.lead: the 1554 siege of kiso-fukushima was a siege by takeda shingen on fukushima castle, in the kiso river valley of shinano province.

entries.label: Siege of Klis
entries.lead: the siege of klis or battle of klis was a siege of klis fortress in the kingdom of croatia within habsburg monarchy.

entries.label: Siege of Knin
entries.lead: the siege of knin was a siege of the city of knin, the capital of the kingdom of croatia, by the ottoman empire in 1522.

entries.label: Siege of Kojinyama
entries.lead: in the 1544 siege of kojinyama, takeda shingen continued his invasion of shinano province's ima valley, seizing kojinyama fortress from the tozawa family.

entries.label: Siege of Kolberg (1807)
entries.lead: the siege of kolberg took place from march to 2 july 1807 during the war of the fourth coalition, part of the napoleonic wars.

entries.label: Siege of Kolberg (Seven Years' War)
entries.lead: during the seven years' war, the prussian-held town of kolberg in brandenburg-prussian pomerania was besieged by russian forces three times.
terms: cerco de kolberg (guerra dos sete anos)

entries.label: Siege of Kolding (1658)
entries.lead: the siege of kolding was fought on december 25, 1658, between sweden and the forces of the polish–lithuanian commonwealth and denmark–norway.

entries.label: Siege of Koppal
entries.lead: the siege of koppal was conducted during the third anglo-mysore war by forces of the nizam of hyderabad under the command of mahabat jung, assisted by a contingent of british east india company forces.

entries.label: Siege of Kőszeg
entries.lead: the siege of koszeg or siege of guns, also known as the german campaign was a siege of koszeg in the western kingdom of hungary which ruled by ferdinand i, a habsburg king, that took place in 1532.

entries.label: Siege of Kōzuki Castle
entries.lead: the siege of kozuki castle occurred in 1578, when the army of mori terumoto attacked and captured the castle of kozuki in harima province.

entries.label: Siege of Kraków
entries.lead: the siege of krakow was one of the battles during the swedish invasion of polish–lithuanian commonwealth.

entries.label: Siege of Kreuznach
entries.lead: the siege of kreuznach or the spanish capture of kreuznach took place on 10 september 1620, at kreuznach in the palatinate, where the army of flanders, led by the spanish don ambrosio spinola, defeated the troops of frederick v, elector of the palatinate, during the palatinate campaign of the thirty

entries.label: Siege of Krujë (1450)
entries.lead: the first siege of kruje occurred in 1450 when an ottoman army led by sultan murad ii and his crown prince mehmed ii tried to besiege the albanian town of kruje.

entries.label: Siege of Krujë (1466–1467)
entries.lead: the second siege of kruje took place from june 1466 to 23 april 1467.

entries.label: Siege of Krujë (1477–1478)
entries.lead: the fourth siege of kruje was an ottoman siege of the venetian-held fortress of kruje in albania from spring 1477 until 16 june 1478.

entries.label: Siege of Kumamoto Castle
entries.lead: the siege of kumamoto castle from february 19 to april 12, 1877, in kumamoto, japan, was a major battle of the satsuma rebellion.

entries.label: Siege of Kuragano
entries.lead: the 1565 siege of kuragano was one of many battles fought during takeda shingen's quest for power during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Kuwabara
entries.lead: the siege of kuwabara took place the day after the siege of uehara; takeda shingen continued to gain power in shinano province by seizing kuwabara castle from suwa yorishige.

entries.label: Siege of La Rochelle
entries.lead: the siege of la rochelle was a result of a war between the french royal forces of king louis xiii and the huguenots of la rochelle in 1627–1628.

entries.label: Siege of La Rochelle (1572–1573)
entries.lead: the siege of la rochelle of 1572–1573 was a massive military assault on the huguenot city of la rochelle by catholic troops during the fourth phase of the french wars of religion, following the august 1572 st.

entries.label: Siege of Ladysmith
entries.lead: the siege of ladysmith was a protracted engagement in the second boer war, taking place between 2 november 1899 and 28 february 1900 at ladysmith, natal.

entries.label: Siege of Laghouat
entries.lead: the siege of laghouat was an episode of the french pacification of algeria.

entries.label: Siege of Laholm Castle
entries.lead: the siege of laholm castle occurred from 2 to 15 may 1644 during gustav horn's invasion of scania, as part of the torstenson war.

entries.label: Siege of Lahore (1761)
entries.lead: the siege of lahore took place in 1761 when the sikhs besieged lahore and captured it after facing no opposition from durrani forces.

entries.label: Siege of Landau (1702)
entries.lead: the siege of landau took place from 16 june to 12 september 1702, during the war of the spanish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Landskrona Citadel
entries.lead: the siege of landskrona citadel occurred from 31 march to 7 april during gustav horn's invasion of scania, in the torstenson war.

entries.label: Siege of Lankaran
entries.lead: the siege of lankaran took place from 7 january to 13 january 1813 during the russo-persian war (1804–1813).

entries.label: Siege of Larache (1689)
entries.lead: the siege of larache, in 1689, was undertaken by an army of morocco under 'alawid sultan ismail ibn sharif against the spanish forces of charles ii, which had ruled the city for almost 80 years since its cession in 1610.

entries.label: Siege of Leiden
entries.lead: the siege of leiden occurred during the eighty years' war in 1573 and 1574, when the spanish under francisco de valdez attempted to capture the rebellious city of leiden, south holland, the netherlands.

entries.label: Siege of Leith
entries.lead: the siege of leith ended a twelve-year encampment of french troops at leith, the port near edinburgh, scotland.

entries.label: Siege of Lens
entries.lead: the siege of lens was an episode of the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Lérida
entries.lead: in the siege of lerida from 29 april to 13 may 1810, an imperial french army under general suchet besieged a spanish garrison led by major general garcia conde.

entries.label: Siege of Leuven
entries.lead: the siege of leuven was an important siege in the thirty years' war in which a franco-dutch army under frederick henry of orange and the french marshals urbain de maille-breze and gaspard iii de coligny, who had invaded the spanish netherlands from two sides, laid siege to the city of leuven, defend

entries.label: Siege of Léva
