entries.label: Siege of Lille (1667)
entries.lead: the siege of lille took place during the war of devolution.

entries.label: Siege of Lille (1708)
entries.lead: the siege of lille was the main operation of the 1708 campaign season during the war of the spanish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Lille (1792)
entries.lead: the siege of lille saw a republican french garrison under jean-baptiste andre ruault de la bonnerie hold lille against an assault by a habsburg army commanded by duke albert of saxe-teschen.

entries.label: Siege of Limerick (1690)
entries.lead: limerick, a city in western ireland, was besieged twice in the williamite war in ireland in 1689–1691.

entries.label: Siege of Limerick (1691)
entries.lead: the siege of limerick in western ireland was a second siege of the town during the williamite war in ireland (1689–1691).

entries.label: Siege of Livadeia
entries.lead: the siege of livadeia was a military engagement of the greek war of independence.

entries.label: Siege of Lons-le-Saunier
entries.lead: the siege of lons-le-saunier was a siege that took place from around 4 june to 2 july 1637 during the ten years' war, the franche-comte episode of the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Louisbourg (1745)
entries.lead: the siege of louisbourg was the 1745 capture of the french settlement of louisbourg on present-day cape breton island, nova scotia, by british north american forces during the war of the austrian succession, known as king george's war in the british colonies.

entries.label: Siege of Louisbourg (1758)
entries.lead: the siege of louisbourg was fought during the seven years' war on cape breton island between an attacking british force and defending french and mi'kmaq troops.

entries.label: Siege of Lucknow
entries.lead: the siege of lucknow was the prolonged defence of the british residency within the city of lucknow from rebel sepoys during the indian rebellion of 1857.

entries.label: Siege of Luxembourg (1684)
entries.lead: the siege of luxembourg, in which louis xiv of france laid siege to the spanish-controlled fortress of luxembourg from 27 april to 7 june 1684, was the most significant confrontation of the war of the reunions between france and spain.

entries.label: Siege of Luxembourg (1794–1795)
entries.lead: the siege of luxembourg was a siege by france of the habsburg-held fortress of luxembourg that lasted from 1794 until 7 june 1795, during the french revolutionary wars.

entries.label: Siege of Lyakhavichy
entries.lead: the siege of lyakhavichy or lachowicze took place from 23 march to 28 june 1660 during the russo-polish war (1654–67).

entries.label: Siege of Lydenburg
entries.lead: the siege of lydenburg was a siege carried out by south african republican forces on british-occupied lydenburg, between january and march 1881 during the first boer war.

entries.label: Siege of Lyon
entries.lead: the siege of lyon occurred on 9 august to 9 october 1793 when french republican forces laid siege and captured the city of lyon, which was the centre of a revolt against the french government during the war of the first coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Maastricht (1579)
entries.lead: the siege of maastricht was a battle of the eighty years' war which lasted from march 12 to july 1, 1579.

entries.label: Siege of Maastricht (1673)
entries.lead: the siege of maastricht, 13 to 30 june 1673, took place during the franco-dutch war, when a french army captured the strategic dutch fortress of maastricht on the meuse river.

entries.label: Siege of Maastricht (1676)
entries.lead: the siege of maastricht (1676) took place from 6 july to 27 august 1676 during the 1672 to 1678 franco-dutch war.

entries.label: Siege of Maastricht (1748)
entries.lead: the siege of maastricht was a campaign during the war of the austrian succession which took place in april–may 1748.

entries.label: Siege of Madras
entries.lead: madras, held by the british, was besieged between december 1758 and february 1759 by french forces under the command of comte de lally during the seven years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Mafeking
entries.lead: the siege of mafeking was a 217-day siege battle for the town of mafeking in south africa during the second boer war from october 1899 to may 1900.

entries.label: Siege of Magdeburg (1806)
entries.lead: the siege of magdeburg took place from 25 october to 8 november 1806 during the war of the fourth coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Mainz (1792)
entries.lead: the siege of mainz was a short engagement at the beginning of the war of the first coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Mainz (1793)
entries.lead: in the siege of mainz, from 14 april to 23 july 1793, a coalition of prussia, austria, and other german states led by the holy roman empire besieged and captured mainz from revolutionary french forces.

entries.label: Siege of Malacca (1551)
entries.lead: the siege of malacca of 1551 was a military engagement that took place in the malay peninsula, between the portuguese empire and the allied forces of the sultanate of johor, the sultanate of pahang, the sultanate of perak and the sultanate of jepara in java.

entries.label: Siege of Malacca (1568)
entries.lead: the siege of malacca occurred in 1568, when the sultan of aceh alauddin attacked the portuguese-held city of malacca.

entries.label: Siege of Malacca (1573)
entries.lead: the siege of malacca occurred in 1573, when the sultan of aceh attacked the portuguese city of malacca with the support of the sultanate of golconda and kalinyamat.

entries.label: Siege of Malacca (1574)
entries.lead: the siege of malacca (1574) was a military conflict between the portuguese empire and the javanese under queen kalinyamat.

entries.label: Siege of Malacca (1575)
entries.lead: the siege of malacca occurred in 1575, when the sultan of aceh attacked the portuguese city of malacca.

entries.label: Siege of Malacca (1606)
entries.lead: the siege of malacca of 1606 was a military engagement between a dutch force commanded by cornelis matelief and the portuguese commander andre furtado de mendonca.

entries.label: Siege of Malacca (1640–1641)
entries.lead: the siege of malacca was initiated by the dutch east india company and their local ally, johor, against portuguese malacca.

entries.label: Siege of Málaga (1487)
entries.lead: the 1487 siege of malaga was an action during the reconquest of spain in which the catholic monarchs of spain conquered the city of malaqa from the emirate of granada.

entries.label: Siege of Malakand
entries.lead: the siege of malakand was the 26 july – 2 august 1897 siege of the british garrison in the malakand region of colonial british india's north west frontier province.

entries.label: Siege of Malmö
entries.lead: the siege of malmo was an unsuccessful danish siege on the swedish-held city of malmo, fought between june 11 and july 5, 1677.

entries.label: Siege of Malta (1429)
entries.lead: the siege of malta, also known as the siege of mdina, was a hafsid invasion of the island of malta, then part of the kingdom of sicily, in september and october 1429.

entries.label: Siege of Malta (1798–1800)
entries.lead: the siege of malta, also known as the siege of valletta or the french blockade, was a two-year siege and blockade of the french garrison in valletta and the three cities, the largest settlements and main port on the mediterranean island of malta, between 1798 and 1800.

entries.label: Siege of Mantua (1796–1797)
entries.lead: the siege of mantua lasted from 4 june 1796 to 2 february 1797 with a short break where french forces under the overall command of napoleon bonaparte besieged and blockaded a large austrian garrison at mantua for many months until it surrendered.

entries.label: Siege of Marabastad
entries.lead: the siege of marabastad was a siege of fort marabastad, in present day limpopo, south africa, carried out by the boer republic of transvaal, starting on 11 january 1881, and ending with british surrender on 2 april 1881.

entries.label: Siege of Marseille (1524)
entries.lead: the siege of marseille (1524) was conducted in august and september 1524 as part of a larger conflict known as the italian war of 1521–1526 by a habsburg army, commanded by the frenchman charles de bourbon and the spaniard fernando de avalos.

entries.label: Siege of Marune
entries.lead: the siege of marune (丸根砦の戦い) was a battle during the sengoku period of japan.

entries.label: Siege of Masbate
entries.lead: the siege of masbate was fought on 19 august 1898, on masbate island as a part of the philippine revolution.

entries.label: Siege of Masulipatam
entries.lead: the siege of masulipatam was a british siege of the town of masulipatam, held by the french and dutch, in india during the seven years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Matsuo
entries.lead: the 1554 siege of matsuo was one of many sieges undertaken by the daimyo takeda shingen in his campaign to conquer japan's shinano province.

entries.label: Siege of Mazagan (1562)
entries.lead: the siege of mazagan of 1562, also known as the great siege of mazagan was an armed engagement that took place in the modern city of el jadida, then known as mazagan, between portuguese forces and those of the saadi dynasty, which had unified morocco a few years prior.

entries.label: Siege of Mazagan (1769)
entries.lead: the siege of mazagan of 1769 was the last engagement between morocco and the portuguese in mazagan.

entries.label: Siege of Meaux
entries.lead: the siege of meaux was fought from october 1421 to may 1422 between the english and the french during the hundred years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Medina Fort
entries.lead: the siege of fort medina took place in 1857 at medine, on the left bank of the senegal river in present-day mali.

entries.label: Siege of Mekelle
entries.lead: the siege of mekelle, sometimes known as the battle of mekelle, took place in january 1896 during the first italo-ethiopian war.

entries.label: Siege of Melilla (1774–1775)
entries.lead: the siege of melilla was an attempt by the sultanate of morocco, supported by algerian mercenaries, to capture the spanish fortress of melilla on the moroccan mediterranean coast.

entries.label: Siege of Memmingen
entries.lead: the siege of memmingen was conducted by bavarian troops under the command of adrian von enkevort.

entries.label: Siege of Mequinenza
entries.lead: the siege of mequinenza saw a 16,000-man imperial french corps commanded by louis gabriel suchet invest a 1,000-strong spanish garrison under colonel carbon.

entries.label: Siege of Metz (1552)
entries.lead: the siege of metz during the italian war of 1551–59 lasted from 19 october 1552 to 2 january 1553.

entries.label: Siege of Metz (1870)
entries.lead: the siege of metz was a siege fought during the franco-prussian war from 19 august to 27 october 1870, and ended in a decisive allied german victory.

entries.label: Siege of Mézières
entries.lead: the siege of mezieres took place in 1521, during the italian war of 1521–1526.

entries.label: Siege of Middelburg (1572–1574)
entries.lead: the siege of middelburg (1572–1574) lasted over a year during the eighty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Miki
entries.lead: the siege of miki (三木合戦) lasted from 1578 to 1580.

entries.label: Siege of Minden
entries.lead: the siege of minden was a siege during the swedish intervention in the thirty years' war involving action between a swedish-luneburg army and an imperial army.

entries.label: Siege of Minowa
entries.lead: the 1566 siege of minowa was one of several battles fought by the takeda clan in their campaigns to seize the lands of the uesugi clan, during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Mirandola (1511)
entries.lead: the siege of mirandola took place from 2 january to 19 january 1511 as a part of pope julius ii's campaign to keep france from dominating northern italy during the war of the league of cambrai.

entries.label: Siege of Mitsuji
entries.lead: the 1576 siege of mitsuji was part of the eleven-year ishiyama hongan-ji war.

entries.label: Siege of Mitú
entries.lead: from 3 to 5 november 1998 during the colombian conflict, rebels belonging to the revolutionary armed forces of colombia (farc) laid siege to the colombian village of mitu, vaupes department.

entries.label: Siege of Moji
entries.lead: the siege of moji was a siege in 1561 of the castle of moji in japan.

entries.label: Siege of Mombasa (1696–1698)
entries.lead: the siege of mombasa was an attack on the portuguese city of mombasa and fort jesus by the army of the ya'rubid ruler of oman, saif i bin sultan, from 13 march 1696 to 13 december 1698.

entries.label: Siege of Monemvasia (1821)
entries.lead: the siege of monemvasia was a military engagement of the greek war of independence, aimed at liberating monemvasia, shortly before the outbreak of the revolution.

entries.label: Siege of Mons (1572)
entries.lead: the siege of mons of 1572 took place at mons, capital of the county of hainaut, spanish netherlands, between 23 june and 19 september 1572, as part of the eighty years' war and the french wars of religion.

entries.label: Siege of Mons (1691)
entries.lead: the siege of mons, 15 march – 10 april 1691, was a major operation fought during the nine years' war, and was the main french objective for the 1691 campaign in the spanish netherlands.

entries.label: Siege of Montargis
entries.lead: the siege of montargis took place during the hundred years war.

entries.label: Siege of Montauban
entries.lead: the siege of montauban was a siege conducted by the young french king louis xiii from august to november 1621, against the protestant stronghold of montauban.

entries.label: Siege of Montevideo (1823)
entries.lead: the siege of montevideo occurred during the brazilian war of independence, during which the brazilian army under carlos frederico lecor attempted to capture the city of montevideo in cisplatina from the portuguese army of alvaro da costa de sousa de macedo.

entries.label: Siege of Montpellier
entries.lead: the siege of montpellier was a siege of the huguenot city of montpellier by the catholic forces of louis xiii of france, from august to october 1622.

entries.label: Siege of Moscow (1618)
entries.lead: the siege of moscow was the last major military action of władysław iv vasa's campaign of 1617–1618 and the entire polish–russian war of 1609–1618.

entries.label: Siege of Mosul (1517)
entries.lead: 1517 siege"

entries.label: Siege of Mosul (1743)
entries.lead: the siege of mosul was the siege of the city of mosul in ottoman iraq by nader shah's army during the persian invasion of the ottoman empire in 1743.

entries.label: Siege of Mount Hiei
entries.lead: the siege of mount hiei was a battle of the sengoku period of japan fought between oda nobunaga and the sohei of the monasteries of enryaku-ji on mount hiei near kyoto on september 30, 1571.

entries.label: Siege of Mozambique (1607)
entries.lead: the 1607 siege of mozambique was an armed encounter between the forces of the portuguese empire and those of the dutch east india company or voc, who attempted to capture the portuguese fort sao sebastiao on the island of mozambique.

entries.label: Siege of Mozambique (1608)
entries.lead: the siege of mozambique of 1608 was a second, unsuccessful, attack by the dutch east india company on the portuguese fortress of mozambique, on the island of mozambique, in 1608.

entries.label: Siege of Multan (1818)
entries.lead: the siege of multan was the final sikh campaign against multan in 1818, resulting in the defeat of muzaffar khan sadozai and the annexation of multan by ranjit singh.

entries.label: Siege of Multan (1848–1849)
entries.lead: the siege of multan began on 19 april 1848 and lasted until 22 january 1849, and saw fighting around multan between the british east india company and the sikh empire.

entries.label: Siege of Musashi-Matsuyama (1537)
entries.lead: the 1537 siege of musashi-matsuyama was the first of several sieges of matsuyama castle in japan's musashi province over the course of the sengoku period (1467-1603).

entries.label: Siege of Musashi-Matsuyama (1563)
entries.lead: in japanese history, the 1563 siege of musashi-matsuyama was a successful attempt by a combined takeda clan-hojo clan army to regain musashi province and matsuyama castle from the uesugi clan; the hojo had seized the castle from the uesugi in the first siege of musashi-matsuyama (1537) but lost it,

entries.label: Siege of Nagakubo
entries.lead: the siege of nagakubo (長窪城) was a battle of japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Namur (1692)
entries.lead: the siege of namur, 25 may–30 june 1692, was a major engagement of the nine years' war, and was part of the french grand plan to defeat the forces of the grand alliance and bring a swift conclusion to the war.

entries.label: Siege of Namur (1695)
entries.lead: the siege of namur took place during the nine years' war between 2 july and 4 september 1695.

entries.label: Siege of Namur (1746)
entries.lead: the siege of namur took place between 6 and 30 september 1746, during the war of the austrian succession.

entries.label: Siege of Namwon
entries.lead: the siege of namwon was a military engagement that occurred from 23 september to 26 september 1597.

entries.label: Siege of Nanao
entries.lead: the siege of nanao was one of many sieges undertaken by uesugi kenshin, an uesugi clan daimyo of japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Naples (1528)
entries.lead: the siege of naples was a siege of the italian city of naples in 1528 during the war of the league of cognac.

entries.label: Siege of Narva (1581)
entries.lead: the siege of narva was a siege and massacre initiated by pontus de la gardie against the russian-controlled city of narva in present-day estonia.

entries.label: Siege of Narva (1704)
entries.lead: the siege of narva, also known as the second battle of narva, was the second russian siege of swedish narva during the great northern war from 8 july to 20 august 1704.

entries.label: Siege of Navarino (1572)
entries.lead: the siege of navarino was a military engagement between the holy league fleet, led by john of austria, who besieged the ottoman garrison in navarino as part of an operation to destroy the ottoman fleet built after the battle of lepanto.

entries.label: Siege of Neamț Citadel
entries.lead: the siege of neamt citadel took place during the moldavian–ottoman war.

entries.label: Siege of Negapatam
entries.lead: the siege of negapatam was the first major offensive military action on the indian subcontinent following the arrival of news that war had been declared between great britain and the dutch republic, beginning the fourth anglo-dutch war.

entries.label: Siege of Negroponte (1470)
entries.lead: the siege of negroponte was fought between the forces of the ottoman empire, led by sultan mehmed ii in person, and the garrison of the venetian colony of negroponte (chalcis), the capital of the venetian possession of euboea in central greece.

entries.label: Siege of Neuss
entries.lead: the siege of neuss, from 1474–75, was linked to the cologne diocesan feud and part of the burgundian wars.

entries.label: Siege of Nice
entries.lead: the siege of nice occurred in 1543 and was part of the italian war of 1542–46 in which francis i and suleiman the magnificent collaborated as part of the franco-ottoman alliance against the holy roman emperor charles v, and henry viii of england.

entries.label: Siege of Nice (1705)
entries.lead: the siege of nice took place between 15 march 1705 and 4 january 1706 as part of the war of the spanish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Nishapur (1755)
entries.lead: the siege of nishapur began in 1755 when ahmad shah durrani, ruler of the durrani empire, invaded khorasan.

entries.label: Siege of Noda Castle
entries.lead: the siege of noda castle (野田城の戦い) took place from january to february 1573, between the forces of the takeda clan, led by takeda shingen, against the tokugawa clan, led by tokugawa ieyasu.

entries.label: Siege of Nöteborg (1702)
entries.lead: the siege of noteborg was one of the first sieges of the great northern war, when russian forces captured the swedish fortress of noteborg in october 1702.

entries.label: Siege of Novi Zrin (1664)
entries.lead: the siege of novi zrin ; croatian: utvrda novi zrin; hungarian: uj-zrinyivar; turkish: zerinvar) in june/july 1664 was last of the military conflicts between the croatian forces led by nikola zrinski, ban (viceroy) of croatia, and the ottoman army commanded by koprulu fazıl ahmed pasha, grand vizier

entries.label: Siege of Nundydroog
entries.lead: the siege of nundydroog was conducted by british indian forces under the command of general charles cornwallis in october 1791, during the third anglo-mysore war.

entries.label: Siege of Nuremberg
entries.lead: the siege of nuremberg was a campaign that took place in 1632 about the imperial city of nuremberg during the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Ochakov (1737)
entries.lead: the siege of ochakov (1737) took place during the austro-russian–turkish war (1735–39) in which the russian army, led by burkhard christoph von munnich, captured the ottoman fortress of ochakov.

entries.label: Siege of Ochakov (1788)
entries.lead: the siege of ochakov or the siege of ozi, now ochakiv, ukraine, was one of the major events of the russo-turkish war (1787–1792).

entries.label: Siege of Odani Castle
entries.lead: the 1573 siege of odani castle was the last stand of the azai clan, one of oda nobunaga's chief opponents.

entries.label: Siege of Odawara (1561)
entries.lead: in the 1561 siege of odawara, a battle of japan's sengoku period, uesugi kenshin attacked odawara castle.

entries.label: Siege of Odawara (1569)
entries.lead: the second siege of odawara took place in 1569.

entries.label: Siege of Odawara (1590)
entries.lead: the third siege of odawara occurred in 1590, and was the primary action in toyotomi hideyoshi's campaign to eliminate the hojo clan as a threat to his power.

entries.label: Siege of Olomouc
entries.lead: the siege of olomouc took place in 1758 when a prussian army led by frederick the great besieged the austrian city of olmutz during the prussian invasion of moravia in the third silesian war.

entries.label: Siege of Đông Quan
entries.lead: 1418 siege"

entries.label: Siege of Oran (1556)
entries.lead: the siege of oran of 1556 occurred when ottoman troops from algiers besieged the spanish garrison in oran.

entries.label: Siege of Oran (1693)
entries.lead: the siege of oran (1693) was an attempt by the alaouite sultan ismail ibn sharif to take the city of oran, which was then under spanish rule.

entries.label: Siege of Oran (1700-1701)
entries.lead: the siege of oran (1700-1701) was an attempt made by moulay ismail to liberate the fortified city of oran from its spanish yoke and annex it to his own kingdom.

entries.label: Siege of Orléans (1428–1429)
entries.lead: the siege of orleans marked a turning point of the hundred years' war between france and england.

entries.label: Siege of Orléans (1563)
entries.lead: the siege of orleans was the final key military engagement of the first french war of religion.

entries.label: Siege of Osaka
entries.lead: the siege of osaka was a series of battles undertaken by the japanese tokugawa shogunate against the toyotomi clan, ending in that clan's destruction.

entries.label: Siege of Oshi
entries.lead: the 1590 siege of oshi was one of many battles in toyotomi hideyoshi's campaigns against the hojo clan during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Ostend
entries.lead: the siege of ostend was a three-year siege of the city of ostend during the eighty years' war and the anglo–spanish war.

entries.label: Siege of Ōta Castle
entries.lead: the 1585 siege of ota castle was one of a series of assaults made by toyotomi hideyoshi against the ikko-ikki religious zealots towards the end of japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Otate
entries.lead: the 1578 siege of otate took place following the sudden death of uesugi kenshin.

entries.label: Siege of Ōtsu
entries.lead: the siege of otsu took place in 1600, concurrent with the battle of sekigahara.

entries.label: Siege of Padua
entries.lead: the siege of padua was a major engagement early in the war of the league of cambrai.

entries.label: Siege of Panhala (1701)
entries.lead: the siege of panhala in 1701 was a significant military expedition led by mughal emperor aurangzeb during his campaign against the marathas.

entries.label: Siege of Paris (1429)
entries.lead: the siege of paris was an assault undertaken in september 1429 during the hundred years' war by the troops of the recently crowned king charles vii of france, with the notable presence of joan of arc, to take the city held by the english and burgundians.

entries.label: Siege of Paris (1590)
entries.lead: the siege of paris took place during the french wars of religion when the french royal army under henry of navarre, and supported by the huguenots, failed to capture the city of paris from the catholic league.

entries.label: Siege of Paris (1870–1871)
entries.lead: the siege of paris took place from 19 september 1870 to 28 january 1871 and ended in the capture of the city by forces of the various states of the north german confederation, led by the kingdom of prussia.

entries.label: Siege of Pärnu
entries.lead: the siege of parnu took place between february 28 and march 2, 1609 during the polish–swedish war (1600–1611).

entries.label: Siege of Patras (1821)
entries.lead: the siege of patras was one of the first events of the greek war of independence.

entries.label: Siege of Paysandú
entries.lead: the siege of paysandu began on 3 december 1864, during the uruguayan war, when brazilian forces and colorado forces attempted to capture the city of paysandu in uruguay from its uruguayan army defenders.

entries.label: Siege of Pécs (1686)
entries.lead: the siege of pecs was fought from 14 to 22 october 1686, in the city of pecs in southwestern hungary, between the armies of the ottoman empire and of the holy roman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Pemaquid (1689)
entries.lead: the siege of pemaquid was a successful attack by a large band of abenaki indians on the english fort at pemaquid, fort charles, then the easternmost outpost of colonial massachusetts.

entries.label: Siege of Pemaquid (1696)
entries.lead: the siege of pemaquid occurred during king william's war when french and native forces from new france attacked the english settlement at pemaquid, a community on the border with acadia.

entries.label: Siege of Pensacola
entries.lead: the siege of pensacola, fought from march 9 to may 10, 1781, was the culmination of spain's conquest of west florida during the gulf coast campaign of the american revolutionary war.

entries.label: Siege of Pensacola (1707)
entries.lead: the siege of pensacola included two separate attempts in 1707 by english-supported creek indians to capture the town and fortress of pensacola, one of two major settlements in spanish florida.

entries.label: Siege of Perpignan (1542)
entries.lead: the siege of perpignan took place in 1542, at perpignan, between a larger french army commanded by henry, dauphin of france and the spanish garrison at perpignan.

entries.label: Siege of Pest
entries.lead: the siege of pest occurred in 1542, when ferdinand i attempted to recover the cities of buda and pest in 1542 from the ottoman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Petersburg
entries.lead: the richmond–petersburg campaign was a series of battles around petersburg, virginia, fought from june 9, 1864, to march 25, 1865, during the american civil war.

entries.label: Siege of Petropavlovsk
entries.lead: the siege of petropavlovsk was a military operation in the pacific theatre of the crimean war in which british and french naval forces unsuccessfully attempted to capture the russian port of petropavlovsk on the kamchatka peninsula.

entries.label: Siege of Philippsburg (1644)
entries.lead: the siege of philippsburg was a french siege of the rhine fortress of philippsburg during the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Philippsburg (1734)
entries.lead: the siege of philippsburg was conducted by french forces against troops of the holy roman empire in the fortress of philippsburg in the rhine river valley during the war of the polish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Pilsen
entries.lead: the siege of pilsen, 19 september to 21 november 1618, was the first significant action of the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Pirna
entries.lead: the siege of pirna, sometimes referred to as the investment of pirna, took place from 10 september to 14 october 1756 as part of the prussian invasion of saxony during the third silesian war.

entries.label: Siege of Pizzighettone
entries.lead: the siege of pizzighettone was the first major military engagement of the northern italian campaigns of the war of the polish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Plevna
entries.lead: the siege of plevna or pleven, was a major battle of the russo-turkish war of 1877–1878, fought by the joint army of the russian empire and the kingdom of romania against the ottoman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Polotsk
entries.lead: the siege of polotsk was laid in 1518 by forces of the grand duchy of moscow on polotsk during the fourth muscovite–lithuanian war (1512–1522).

entries.label: Siege of Pondicherry (1748)
entries.lead: the siege of pondicherry was conducted by british forces against a french east india company garrison under the command of governor-general joseph francois dupleix at the indian port of pondicherry.

entries.label: Siege of Pondicherry (1760)
entries.lead: the siege of pondicherry (1760–1761) was a conflict in the third carnatic war, as part of the global seven years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Pondicherry (1778)
entries.lead: the siege of pondicherry was the first military action on the indian subcontinent following the declaration of war between great britain and france in the american revolutionary war.

entries.label: Siege of Pondicherry (1793)
entries.lead: the siege of pondicherry was a colonial military operation in the early stages of the french revolutionary wars.

entries.label: Siege of Port Arthur
entries.lead: the siege of port arthur was the longest and most violent land battle of the russo-japanese war.

entries.label: Siege of Port-au-Prince (1793)
entries.lead: the siege of port-au-prince took place in april 1793 during the haitian revolution.

entries.label: Siege of Port-au-Prince (1803)
entries.lead: the siege of port-au-prince was an engagement that took place from october to november 1803 during the haitian revolution.

entries.label: Siege of Port Hudson
entries.lead: the siege of port hudson was the final engagement in the union campaign to recapture the mississippi river in the american civil war.

entries.label: Siege of Port Royal (1710)
entries.lead: the siege of port royal, also known as the conquest of acadia, was a military siege conducted by british regular and provincial forces under the command of francis nicholson against a french acadian garrison and the wabanaki confederacy under the command of daniel d'auger de subercase, at the acadia

entries.label: Siege of Prague
entries.lead: the siege of prague was an unsuccessful attempt by a prussian army led by frederick the great to capture the bohemian city of prague during the third silesian war.

entries.label: Siege of Prague (1742)
entries.lead: the 1742 siege of prague was an extended blockade of the bohemian capital during the war of the austrian succession.

entries.label: Siege of Prague (1744)
entries.lead: the siege of prague resulted in the surrender of the habsburg austrian garrison of prague during the bohemian campaign of 1744 in the war of the austrian succession.

entries.label: Siege of Privas
entries.lead: the siege of privas was undertaken by louis xiii of france from 14 may 1629, and the city of privas was captured on 28 may 1629.

entries.label: Siege of Pskov
entries.lead: the siege of pskov, known as the pskov defense in russia, took place between august 1581 and february 1582, when the army of the polish king and grand duke of lithuania stephen bathory laid an unsuccessful siege and successful blockade of the city of pskov during the final stage of the livonian war

entries.label: Siege of Puebla (1863)
entries.lead: the siege of puebla occurred between 16 march and 17 may 1863 during the second french intervention in mexico, between forces of the second french empire and forces of the second federal republic of mexico.

entries.label: Siege of Pyongyang (1592)
entries.lead: the siege of pyongyang was part of the japanese invasions of korea.

entries.label: Siege of Pyongyang (1593)
entries.lead: the siege of pyongyang was a military conflict fought between the allied ming-joseon army and the japanese first division under konishi yukinaga, who were besieged in the city of pyongyang.

entries.label: Siege of Qatif (1551)
entries.lead: the siege of qatif was a military confrontation between the portuguese empire and the ottoman empire at qatif in 1551.

entries.label: Siege of Querétaro
entries.lead: the siege of queretaro was the culminating battle of the second french intervention in mexico and the second mexican empire.

entries.label: Siege of Ragusa (1806)
entries.lead: the siege of ragusa took place in 1806 during the napoleonic wars.

entries.label: Siege of Rheinfelden (1633)
entries.lead: the siege of rheinfelden of 1633 or the spanish recapture of rheinfelden (spanish: la expugnacion de rheinfelden) took place in late october 1633, during the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Rhodes (1480)
entries.lead: the siege of rhodes of 1480 was the first and failed attempt by the ottoman empire to seize the island stronghold of the knights of rhodes from rhodes, despite about 70,000 troops, they successfully defended the island.

entries.label: Siege of Rhodes (1522)
entries.lead: the siege of rhodes of 1522 was the second and ultimately successful attempt by the ottoman empire to expel the knights of rhodes from their island stronghold and thereby secure ottoman control of the eastern mediterranean.

entries.label: Siege of Riga (1656)
entries.lead: the siege of riga by the russian army under tsar alexei mikhailovich was the main event of the russo-swedish war.

entries.label: Siege of Riga (1700)
entries.lead: the sieges of riga were two sieges which took place on february 22 and june 15, 1700, in riga during the great northern war.

entries.label: Siege of Roses (1808)
entries.lead: the siege of roses or siege of rosas from 7 november to 5 december 1808 saw an imperial french corps led by laurent gouvion saint-cyr invest a catalan and spanish garrison commanded by peter o'daly.

entries.label: Siege of Rouen (1418–1419)
entries.lead: the siege of rouen was a major event in the hundred years' war, in which english forces loyal to henry v captured rouen, the capital of normandy, from the norman french.

entries.label: Siege of Rouen (1562)
entries.lead: the siege of rouen was a key military engagement of the first french war of religion.

entries.label: Siege of Rouen (1591–1592)
entries.lead: the siege of rouen was an unsuccessful attempt by henry iv of france to capture rouen, the historical capital city of normandy.

entries.label: Siege of Rustenburg
entries.lead: the siege of rustenburg was a siege that took place between 1880 and 1881 during the first boer war.

entries.label: Siege of Ryūgasaki
entries.lead: the 1545 siege of ryugasaki was one of many battles fought by takeda shingen in his bid to control shinano province during japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of 's-Hertogenbosch
entries.lead: the siege of 's-hertogenbosch also known as the siege of bois-le-duc was an action in 1629, during the eighty years' war and the anglo–spanish war in which a dutch army captured the city of 's-hertogenbosch.

entries.label: Siege of Saati
entries.lead: the siege of saati, also known as battle of saati or combat of saati, was the first battle of the italo-ethiopian war of 1887–1889 between italian colonial troops and ethiopian forces.

entries.label: Siege of Šabac (1521)
entries.lead: the siege of sabac or szabacs occurred on 7 july in the year 1521 when the ottoman empire conquered the sabac fortress.

entries.label: Siege of Saigon
entries.lead: the siege of saigon, a two-year siege of the city by the vietnamese after its capture on 17 february 1859 by a franco-spanish flotilla under the command of the french admiral charles rigault de genouilly, was one of the major events of the cochinchina campaign (1858–1862).

entries.label: Siege of Saint-Jean-d'Angély (1621)
entries.lead: the siege of saint-jean-d'angely was a siege, accomplished by the young french king louis xiii in 1621, against the protestant stronghold of saint-jean-d'angely led by rohan's brother benjamin de rohan, duc de soubise.

entries.label: Siege of Saint-Martin-de-Ré
entries.lead: the siege of saint-martin-de-re, or siege of st.

entries.label: Siege of Saint-Omer
entries.lead: the siege of saint-omer was a siege in the thirty years' war in which a french army under gaspard iii de coligny, marechal de chatillon, laid siege to the flemish city of saint-omer, defended by a small garrison in command of lancelot ii schetz, count of grobbendonck.

entries.label: Siege of Salona (1821)
entries.lead: the siege of salona was a military engagement of the 1821 revolution aimed at liberating salona.

entries.label: Siege of Salses
entries.lead: the siege of salses (1639–1640) was a double siege during the franco-spanish war (1635–1659), starting with a french success, but ending with a spanish victory.

entries.label: Siege of Salvador (1638)
entries.lead: the siege of salvador was a siege that took place between april and may 1638, during the dutch–portuguese war and eighty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Salvador (1822–1823)
entries.lead: the siege of salvador occurred during the brazilian war of independence, during which the newly formed brazilian army, under the command of french general pierre labatut, attempted to capture the city of salvador in bahia from its portuguese defenders.

entries.label: Siege of Samarkand (1490s)
entries.lead: the sieges of samarkand (1494-1496) were two failed sieges of samarkand during the chaotic years of civil war that preceded the fall of the timurid empire in 1501.

entries.label: Siege of Samarkand (1497)
entries.lead: the siege of samarkand (1497) was a successful siege by the two armies of emir babur of fergana and sultan ali of bukhara of the city of samarkand.

entries.label: Siege of Samarkand (1501)
entries.lead: the siege of samarkand was the third and last campaign against the city between mughal and uzbeks.

entries.label: Siege of Samarkand (1868)
entries.lead: the siege of samarkand, or siege of the samarkand citadel, was a military engagement fought in the city of samarkand in june 1868.

entries.label: Siege of San Sebastián
entries.lead: the siege of san sebastian took place between 7 july and 8 september 1813, during the peninsular war.

entries.label: Siege of Santa Maura (1684)
entries.lead: the siege of santa maura took place on 21 july – 6 august 1684 between the forces of the republic of venice and the ottoman empire, and was the opening battle of the sixth ottoman–venetian war.

entries.label: Siege of Santiago
entries.lead: the siege of santiago, also known as the siege of santiago de cuba, was the last major operation of the spanish–american war on the island of cuba.

entries.label: Siege of Savannah (1779)
entries.lead: the siege of savannah or the second battle of savannah was an encounter of the american revolutionary war (1775–1783) in 1779.

entries.label: Siege of Schenkenschans
entries.lead: the siege of schenkenschans was a major siege of the eighty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Seringapatam (1799)
entries.lead: the siege of seringapatam was the final confrontation of the fourth anglo-mysore war between the british east india company and the kingdom of mysore led by tipu sultan who ruled after the death of his father.

entries.label: Siege of Sevastopol (1854–1855)
entries.lead: the siege of sevastopol lasted from october 1854 until september 1855, during the crimean war.

entries.label: Siege of Shamakhi
entries.lead: the siege of shamakhi was a phase in the ottoman–safavid war (1603–1612) that resulted in the safavid army's success and shamakhi's return to iranian rule after 28 years.

entries.label: Siege of Shamakhi (1578)
entries.lead: the siege of shamakhi (persian: محاصره شماخی) occurred during the ottoman–safavid war (1578–1590), as an attempt by the safavids to capture the ottoman stronghold of shamakhi in 9-12 november 1578.

entries.label: Siege of Shigisan
entries.lead: in the history of japan, the 1577 siege of shigisan was one of many sieges during oda nobunaga's campaigns to consolidate his power in the kansai area.

entries.label: Siege of Shika Castle
entries.lead: the siege of shika castle, which took place in september 1547, was one of many battles fought in takeda shingen's bid to seize control of shinano province.

entries.label: Siege of Shimoda
entries.lead: the siege of shimoda was a naval siege conducted against a coastal hojo fortress in izu province, part of odawara campaign.

entries.label: Siege of Shiroishi
entries.lead: the siege of shiroishi, in 1600, was one of several feudal japanese battles leading up to the decisive battle of sekigahara which ended the period of over 100 years of war, and was immediately followed by the establishment of the tokugawa shogunate.

entries.label: Siege of Shkodra
entries.lead: the siege of shkodra took place from may 1478 to april 1479 as a confrontation between the ottoman empire and the venetians together with the league of lezhe and other albanians at shkodra and its rozafa castle during the first ottoman-venetian war (1463–1479).

entries.label: Siege of Silistria (1854)
entries.lead: the siege of silistria, or siege of silistra, was a key engagement in the crimean war, fought from 11 may to 23 june 1854 between the russian empire and the ottoman empire in present-day bulgaria.

entries.label: Siege of Smolensk (1502)
entries.lead: the siege of smolensk was an unsuccessful attempt to capture smolensk by the forces of the grand duchy of moscow in summer 1502.

entries.label: Siege of Smolensk (1514)
entries.lead: the siege of smolensk of 1514 took place during the fourth muscovite–lithuanian war (1512–1520).

entries.label: Siege of Smolensk (1609–1611)
entries.lead: the siege of smolensk, also known as the smolensk defense in russia, lasted 20 months between 29 september 1609 to 13 june 1611, when the polish army besieged the russian city of smolensk during the polish–russian war of 1609–1618.

entries.label: Siege of Smolensk (1632–1633)
entries.lead: the siege of smolensk lasted almost a year between 1632 and 1633, when the muscovite army besieged the polish–lithuanian city of smolensk during the war named after that siege.

entries.label: Siege of Smolensk (1654)
entries.lead: the siege of smolensk was one of the first great events of the russo-polish war (1654–67).

entries.label: Siege of Snoghøj
entries.lead: the siege of snoghøj occurred from 11 to 14 january 1644 during the torstenson war between denmark–norway and sweden.

entries.label: Siege of Springfield
entries.lead: the siege of springfield was a siege of the colonial new england settlement of springfield in 1675 by native americans during king philip's war.

entries.label: Siege of St. Augustine (1740)
entries.lead: the siege of st.

entries.label: Siege of St. John's
entries.lead: the siege of st.

entries.label: Siege of Stralsund (1628)
entries.lead: the siege of stralsund, 13 may to 4 august 1628, took place during the thirty years' war when an imperial army under albrecht von wallenstein attempted to capture the key baltic sea port of stralsund.

entries.label: Siege of Stralsund (1678)
entries.lead: the siege of stralsund was an armed engagement between the electorate of brandenburg and the swedish empire from 20 september to 15 october 1678, during the scanian war.

entries.label: Siege of Stralsund (1711–1715)
entries.lead: the siege of stralsund was an armed engagement during the great northern war.

entries.label: Siege of Stralsund (1807)
entries.lead: the siege of stralsund lasted from 24 july to 24 august, 1807, and saw troops from the first french empire twice attempt to capture the port city from lieutenant general hans henric von essen's 15,000-man swedish garrison.

entries.label: Siege of Strasbourg
entries.lead: the siege of strasbourg took place during the franco-prussian war, and resulted in the french surrender of the fortress on 28 september 1870.

entries.label: Siege of Suemori
entries.lead: the siege of suemori was a battle during the azuchi–momoyama period of japan.

entries.label: Siege of Suffolk
entries.lead: the siege of suffolk, also known as the battle of suffolk, took place from april 11 to may 4, 1863, near suffolk, virginia during the american civil war.

entries.label: Siege of Suncheon
entries.lead: the siege of suncheon or siege of japanese fortress was an unsuccessful korean and chinese allied forces attempt to capture suncheon japanese castle late in the japanese invasions of korea (1592–1598).

entries.label: Siege of Suzhou
entries.lead: the battle of suzhou was fought on 6 december 1863 between the anglo-qing army and the taiping army.

entries.label: Siege of Svetigrad
entries.lead: the siege of svetigrad or sfetigrad began on 14 may 1448 when an ottoman army, led by sultan murad ii, besieged the fortress of svetigrad.

entries.label: Siege of Szigetvár
entries.lead: the siege of szigetvar or the battle of szigeth was an ottoman siege of the fortress of szigetvar in the kingdom of hungary.

entries.label: Siege of Tabriz (1501)
entries.lead: the siege of tabriz took place in 1501 just after the safavids had defeated the aq qoyunlu in the battle of sharur.

entries.label: Siege of Taganrog
entries.lead: the siege of taganrog is a name given in some russian histories to anglo-french naval operations in the sea of azov between june and november 1855 during the crimean war.

entries.label: Siege of Taif (1814)
entries.lead: in 1814, in a counter attack during the second campaign of the ottoman–wahhabi war, abdullah bin saud al saud's forces laid siege to the ottoman held city of taif.

entries.label: Siege of Takamatsu
entries.lead: in the 1582 siege of takamatsu , toyotomi hideyoshi laid siege to takamatsu castle, which was controlled by the mori clan.

entries.label: Siege of Takatenjin (1581)
entries.lead: the second siege of takatenjin began only six years after takeda katsuyori had taken the fortress.

entries.label: Siege of Takatō (1545)
entries.lead: the 1545 siege of takato castle, saw takeda shingen continuing his sweep through the ima valley of shinano province, seeking to take control of the entire province.

entries.label: Siege of Takatō (1582)
entries.lead: in the history of japan, the 1582 siege of takato (高遠城の戦い) was one of the final battles of the takeda clan against the forces of oda nobunaga.

entries.label: Siege of Takehana
entries.lead: the 1584 siege of takehana was something of a follow-up to the siege of kaganoi; the great warlord toyotomi hideyoshi sought to consolidate his power, particularly in the lands of his late lord oda nobunaga.

entries.label: Siege of Tanabe
entries.lead: the siege of tanabe in 1600 was one of a number of battles which took place in parallel to the more influential sekigahara campaign, which led to the unification of japan under tokugawa ieyasu.

entries.label: Siege of Tangier (1463–1464)
entries.lead: the siege of tangier (1463–1464) was an attempt by the portuguese, led by afonso v of portugal to capture the city of tangiers.

entries.label: Siege of Tarragona (1811)
entries.lead: in the siege of tarragona, from 5 may to 29 june 1811, louis gabriel suchet's french army of aragon laid siege to a spanish garrison led by lieutenant general juan senen de contreras.

entries.label: Siege of Tashkent
entries.lead: the siege of tashkent was the last major battle between the khanate of kokand and the russian empire during the russo-kokand war.

entries.label: Siege of Tellicherry
entries.lead: the siege of tellicherry was a military embargo that happened in thalassery.

entries.label: Siege of Temesvár (1552)
entries.lead: the siege of temesvar was a military conflict between the habsburg monarchy and the ottoman empire in 1552.

entries.label: Siege of Temeşvar (1716)
entries.lead: the siege of temesvar took place from 31 august to 12 october 1716 during the austro-turkish war of 1716-1718, to liberate the last regions of ottoman-occupied hungary.

entries.label: Siege of Terabe
entries.lead: the siege of terabe castle took place in 1558 in feudal japan.

entries.label: Siege of Tessalit
entries.lead: the siege of tessalit occurred in early 2012 during the tuareg rebellion in mali.

entries.label: Siege of the Acropolis (1687)
entries.lead: the siege of the acropolis took place on 23–29 september 1687, as the venetian forces under francesco morosini and otto wilhelm konigsmarck laid siege to the acropolis of athens, held by the ottoman garrison of the city.

entries.label: Siege of the Acropolis (1821–1822)
entries.lead: the first siege of the acropolis in 1821–1822 was the siege of the acropolis of athens by the greek revolutionary forces, during the early stages of the greek war of independence.

entries.label: Siege of the Acropolis (1826–1827)
entries.lead: the second siege of the acropolis in 1826–1827 during the greek war of independence involved the siege of the acropolis of athens, the last fortress still held by the greek rebels in central greece, by the forces of the ottoman empire.

entries.label: Siege of the British Residency in Kabul
entries.lead: the siege of the british residency in kabul was a military engagement of the second anglo-afghan war.
terms: siege of the british residency in kabul

entries.label: Siege of the Castle of Saint George
entries.lead: the siege of the castle of saint george, also known as the siege of cephalonia, occurred from 8 november until 24 december 1500, when following a series of venetian disasters at the hands of the turks, the spanish-venetian army under captain gonzalo fernandez de cordoba and benedetto pesaro succeede
terms: siege of the castle of saint george

entries.label: Siege of the International Legations
entries.lead: the siege of the international legations was a pivotal event during the boxer rebellion in 1900, in which foreign diplomatic compounds in peking were besieged by chinese boxers and qing dynasty troops.

entries.label: Siege of the Mechouar of Tlemcen
entries.lead: the siege of the mechouar of tlemcen, the citadel of the city, was led by emir abdelkader from 1834 to 1836 against the garrison entrenched within its walls, composed of turks and kouloughlis.
terms: siege of the mechouar of tlemcen

entries.label: Siege of the Sherpur Cantonment
entries.lead: the siege of the sherpur cantonment was a battle fought in december 1879, during the second anglo-afghan war.

entries.label: Siege of Thessalonica (1422–1430)
entries.lead: the siege of thessalonica between 1422 and 1430 saw the ottoman empire, under sultan murad ii, capture the city of thessalonica.

entries.label: Siege of Thionville (1792)
entries.lead: the siege of thionville saw an unsuccessful attempt to conquer the french stronghold of thionville by the austro-royalists during the war of the first coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Thorn (1703)
entries.lead: the siege of thorn was set during the great northern war, between sweden and saxony from 26 may – 14 october 1703 (n.s.?).

entries.label: Siege of Tönning
entries.lead: during the great northern war, the fortress of tonning in the territory of holstein-gottorp, an ally of the swedish empire, was besieged twice.

entries.label: Siege of Tortosa (1810–1811)
entries.lead: the siege of tortosa pitted an imperial french army under general louis gabriel suchet against the spanish defenders of tortosa led by general miguel de lili idiaquez, conde de alacha.

entries.label: Siege of Tottori
entries.lead: the siege of tottori castle occurred in 1581 and was part of oda nobunaga's campaign to consolidate his power in western honshu in an effort to unite japan during the late 16th century.

entries.label: Siege of Toul
entries.lead: the siege of toul was the siege of the fortified french town of toul from 16 august to 23 september 1870 by prussian, bavarian and wurttemberg forces during the franco-prussian war.

entries.label: Siege of Toulon (1707)
entries.lead: the siege of toulon took place between 29 july and 21 august 1707 during the war of the spanish succession, when a combined savoyard-imperial army supported by a anglo-dutch naval force, attacked the french base at toulon.

entries.label: Siege of Toulon (1793)
entries.lead: the siege of toulon took place during the war of the first coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Tourane
entries.lead: the siege of tourane was a vietnamese victory during the cochinchina campaign, a punitive campaign against the vietnamese launched by france and spain in 1858.

entries.label: Siege of Tournai (1745)
entries.lead: the siege of tournai was a two-month siege of the city and citadel of tournai, then part of the austrian netherlands, in 1745 during the war of the austrian succession.

entries.label: Siege of Toyama
entries.lead: the siege of toyama was a battle during the azuchi-momoyama period of japan.

entries.label: Siege of Trarbach
entries.lead: the siege of trarbach was conducted during the war of the polish succession by french troops against a garrison of troops of the holy roman empire in the fortress at trarbach in the county of sponheim, a small principality of the holy roman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Tre Kronor
entries.lead: the siege of tre kronor, or the siege of the royal castle in stockholm, was a siege of the tre kronor castle in stockholm lasting from 17 october 1501 to 9 may 1502 between the kalmar union and sten sture the elder's swedish rebellion.

entries.label: Siege of Trebizond (1461)
entries.lead: the siege of trebizond was the successful siege of the city of trebizond, capital of the empire of trebizond, by the ottomans under sultan mehmed ii, which ended on 15 august 1461.

entries.label: Siege of Trichinopoly (1743)
entries.lead: the siege of trichinopoly was part of an extended series of conflicts between the nizam of hyderabad and the maratha empire for control of the carnatic region.

entries.label: Siege of Tripoli (1551)
entries.lead: the siege of tripoli was a successful ottoman siege of the north african city of tripoli, then held by the knights hospitaller, in august 1551.

entries.label: Siege of Tripoli (1705)
entries.lead: the siege of tripoli was initiated by the tunisian bey, ibrahim al-sharif, who attempted to "wreak his wrath" on the population of tripoli.

entries.label: Siege of Tripolitsa
entries.lead: the siege of tripolitsa or fall of tripolitsa, also known as the tripolitsa massacre, was an early victory of the revolutionary greek forces in the summer of 1821 during the greek war of independence, which had begun earlier that year, against the ottoman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Troitsky monastery
entries.lead: the siege of troitsky monastery was an abortive attempt of the polish–lithuanian irregular army (mercenaries) that acted in support of false dmitry ii to capture the trinity lavra of st.

entries.label: Siege of Turin
entries.lead: the siege of turin, june to september 1706, took place during the war of the spanish succession.

entries.label: Siege of Turin (1640)
entries.lead: the 1640 siege of turin was a major action in two distinct wars: the franco-spanish war (1635–59) and the piedmontese civil war.

entries.label: Siege of Tuyên Quang
entries.lead: the siege of tuyen quang was an important confrontation between the french and the chinese armies in tonkin during the sino-french war.

entries.label: Siege of Uchiyama
entries.lead: the 1546 siege of uchiyama was one of many battles fought by takeda shingen bid to gain control of shinano province.

entries.label: Siege of Ueda
entries.lead: the siege of ueda was staged in 1600 by tokugawa hidetada, son and heir of the warlord tokugawa ieyasu, against ueda castle garrison in shinano province, which was controlled by the sanada family.

entries.label: Siege of Uehara
entries.lead: the siege of uehara was the first of many steps taken by takeda shingen in his bid to seize control of shinano province.

entries.label: Siege of Ulsan
entries.lead: the siege of ulsan was an unsuccessful ming-joseon attempt to capture ulsan from the japanese.

entries.label: Siege of Uozu
entries.lead: the 1582 siege of uozu castle was part of a border dispute between two daimyo of japan's sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Uruguaiana
entries.lead: the siege of uruguaiana was an engagement in the paraguayan war that began in late august 1865, and ended on 18 september that year when the paraguayans were forced to surrender due to low food supplies.

entries.label: Siege of Valencia (1812)
entries.lead: the siege of valencia from 3 november 1811 to 9 january 1812, saw marshal louis gabriel suchet's french army of aragon besiege captain general joaquin blake y joyes's forces in the city of valencia, spain, during the peninsular war.

entries.label: Siege of Valenciennes (1676–1677)
entries.lead: the siege of valenciennes, 28 february to 17 march 1677, took place during the 1672 to 1678 franco-dutch war.

entries.label: Siege of Valenciennes (1793)
entries.lead: the siege of valenciennes took place between 13 june and 28 july 1793, during the flanders campaign of the war of the first coalition.

entries.label: Siege of Van (1548)
entries.lead: the siege of van occurred in 1548 when suleiman the magnificent attacked iran in his second campaign of the ottoman-safavid war (1532–1555).

entries.label: Siege of Varna (1828)
entries.lead: the siege of varna took place during the russo-turkish war, 1828–1829.

entries.label: Siege of Varnakova
entries.lead: the siege of varnakova in 1826 was one of the military episodes of the greek war of independence.

entries.label: Siege of Velikiye Luki
entries.lead: the siege of velikiye luki was one of the battles of livonian campaign of stephen bathory.

entries.label: Siege of Vepryk
entries.lead: the siege of vepryk or veprik took place on 3–18 january 1709 during the poltava campaign in the northern war in ukraine near the ukrainian city of vepryk.

entries.label: Siege of Veracruz
entries.lead: on 9 march 1847, during the mexican–american war, the united states military made an amphibious landing and besieged the key mexican seaport of veracruz.

entries.label: Siege of Viborg (1710)
entries.lead: the siege of viborg took place in the spring of 1710 during the great northern war (1700–1721), as a second attempt by the russians to capture the fortress port of viborg, near the modern border between russia and finland, after a failed attempt in 1706.

entries.label: Siege of Vicksburg
entries.lead: the siege of vicksburg was the final major military action in the vicksburg campaign of the american civil war.

entries.label: Siege of Vienna (1485)
entries.lead: the siege of vienna was a decisive siege in 1485 of the austrian–hungarian war.

entries.label: Siege of Vienna (1529)
entries.lead: the 1529 siege of vienna was the first attempt by the ottoman empire to capture the city of vienna in the archduchy of austria, part of the holy roman empire.

entries.label: Siege of Villafranca (1744)
entries.lead: the siege of villafranca took place between 14 and 27 april 1744, during the war of the austrian succession.

entries.label: Siege of Warsaw (1794)
entries.lead: the siege of warsaw of 1794 was a joint russian and prussian siege of the capital of the polish–lithuanian commonwealth, during the kosciuszko uprising in the summer of 1794.

entries.label: Siege of Weissenstein
entries.lead: the siege of weissenstein took place between 31 may and 30 september 1602, during the polish–swedish war of 1600–1611.

entries.label: Siege of Wesenberg (1574)
entries.lead: the siege of wesenberg, rakvere, or rakovor, was an abortive swedish siege of the russian-held town of wesenberg in estonia from january through march 1574, during the livonian war.

entries.label: Siege of Wolgast (1630)
entries.lead: the siege of wolgast was a swedish siege of the imperial garrison of wolgast during the thirty years' war.

entries.label: Siege of Wolmar
entries.lead: the siege of wolmar occurred during the polish–swedish war (1600–1611), between october 18 and december 18, 1601.

entries.label: Siege of Xàtiva (1707)
entries.lead: the siege of xativa was a siege of xativa in the kingdom of valencia.

entries.label: Siege of Yeongwon
entries.lead: the siege of yeongwon castle took place in 1592 during the japanese invasions of korea.

entries.label: Siege of Yorktown
entries.lead: the siege of yorktown, also known as the battle of yorktown and the surrender at yorktown, took place in 1781 and was the final major land engagement of the american revolutionary war.

entries.label: Siege of Yorktown (1862)
entries.lead: the battle of yorktown or siege of yorktown was fought from april 5 to may 4, 1862, as part of the peninsula campaign of the american civil war.

entries.label: Siege of Yoshida Castle
entries.lead: the 1575 siege of yoshida castle was undertaken by takeda katsuyori against the forces of tokugawa ieyasu during the sengoku period of japanese history.

entries.label: Siege of Yoshida-Kōriyama Castle
entries.lead: the siege of yoshida-koriyama castle took place from 5 october 1540 until 8 february 1541 in yoshida, aki province, japan during the sengoku period.

entries.label: Siege of Ypres (1678)
entries.lead: the siege of ypres in the spanish netherlands took place between march 18 and march 25, 1678, as part of the franco-dutch war, and ended with the conquest of the city by the french.

entries.label: Siege of Zaragoza (1808)
entries.lead: the siege of zaragoza was a bloody struggle in the peninsular war.

entries.label: Siege of Zaragoza (1809)
entries.lead: the siege of zaragoza was the french capture of the spanish city of zaragoza in 1809 during the peninsular war.

entries.label: Siege of Zbarazh
entries.lead: the siege of zbarazh was a part of the khmelnytsky uprising, and occurred in and around the site of the present-day city of zbarazh in ukraine.

entries.label: Siege of Zhvanets
entries.lead: the siege of zhvanets was fought between the cossack hetmanate, crimean khanate and the polish–lithuanian commonwealth as a part of the khmelnytskyi uprising.

entries.label: Siege of Zierikzee
entries.lead: the siege of zierikzee was a siege in the eighty years' war between october 1575 and july 1576.

entries.label: Siege of Zutphen (1591)
entries.lead: the siege of zutphen was an eleven-day siege of the city of zutphen by dutch and english troops led by maurice of nassau, during the eighty years' war and the anglo–spanish war.

entries.label: Sieges of Boulogne (1544–1546)
entries.lead: the sieges of boulogne were two sieges which took place between england and france during the rough wooing and italian war of 1542–1546.

entries.label: Sieges of Ceuta (1694–1727)
entries.lead: the sieges of ceuta, also known as the thirty-year siege, were a series of blockades by moroccan forces of the spanish-held city of ceuta on the north african coast.

entries.label: Sieges of Gassantoda Castle
entries.lead: the sieges of gassantoda castle were a series of 16th-century battles during the sengoku period of japan.

entries.label: Sieges of Nagashima
entries.lead: the sieges of nagashima , taking place in 1571, 1573, and 1574, were part of oda nobunaga's campaigns against the ikko-ikki, arguably among his greatest enemies.

entries.label: Sieges of Oran and Mers El Kébir
entries.lead: the sieges of oran and mers el kebir of 1563 is a major attempt by the regency of algiers to retake the cities of mers el-kebir and oran from the spanish.
terms: sieges of oran and mers el kebir

entries.label: Sieges of Taunton
entries.lead: the sieges of taunton were a series of three blockades during the first english civil war.

entries.label: Sieges of Toishi
entries.lead: the sieges of toishi castle took place during takeda shingen's campaign to take over shinano province.

entries.label: Sierra Leone Civil War

entries.label: Signing of the United States Declaration of Independence
entries.lead: the signing of the united states declaration of independence occurred primarily on august 2, 1776, at the pennsylvania state house, later renamed independence hall, in philadelphia.
terms: signing of the united states declaration of independence
lista dos congressistas signatarios da declaracao da independencia dos estados unidos

entries.label: Sikkim expedition
entries.lead: the sikkim expedition was an 1888 british military expedition to expel tibetan forces from sikkim.

entries.label: Silent Sejm
entries.lead: silent sejm, also known as the mute sejm, is the name given to the session of the sejm parliament of the polish–lithuanian commonwealth of 1 february 1717 held in warsaw.

entries.label: Silesian Wars
entries.lead: the silesian wars were three wars fought in the mid-18th century between prussia, under king frederick the great, and habsburg austria, under empress maria theresa, for control of the central european region of silesia, now in south-western poland.

entries.label: Simba rebellion
entries.lead: the simba rebellion, also known as the orientale revolt, was a regional uprising which took place in the democratic republic of the congo between 1963 and 1965 in the wider context of the congo crisis and the cold war.

entries.label: Singeing the King of Spain's Beard
entries.lead: singeing the king of spain's beard is the derisive name given to attacks by the english privateer francis drake against the spanish in the summer of 1587, beginning in april with a raid on cadiz.
terms: singeing the king of spain's beard

entries.label: Single European Act
entries.lead: the single european act (sea) was the first major revision of the 1957 treaty of rome.

entries.label: Sinhalese–Portuguese conflicts
entries.lead: between 1518 and 1658, armed conflict took place between the native sinhalese kingdoms of sri lanka, and the portuguese empire.

entries.label: Sinking of ARA General Belgrano
entries.lead: the argentine cruiser ara general belgrano was sunk on may 2, 1982, by the british nuclear submarine hms conqueror during the falklands war.

entries.label: Sinking of the Nossa Senhora da Conceição
entries.lead: the sinking of the nossa senhora da conceicao was a naval engagement between the loaded portuguese carrack, commanded by luis de sousa, and a fleet of algerian corsairs in 1621.
terms: sinking of the nossa senhora da conceicao

entries.label: Sino-Burmese War
entries.lead: the sino-burmese war, also known as the qing invasions of burma or the myanmar campaign of the qing dynasty, was a war fought between the qing dynasty of china and the konbaung dynasty of burma (myanmar).

entries.label: Sino-French War
entries.lead: the sino-french or franco-chinese war, also known as the tonkin war, was a limited conflict fought from august 1884 to april 1885 between the french third republic and the qing dynasty for the suzerainty of vietnam.

entries.label: Sino-Indian War
entries.lead: the sino-indian war, also known as the china–india war or the indo-china war, was an armed conflict between china and india that took place from october to november 1962.

entries.label: Sino-Japanese Friendship and Trade Treaty
entries.lead: the sino-japanese friendship and trade treaty was the first treaty between japan and the qing dynasty.

entries.label: Sino-Nepalese War
entries.lead: the sino-nepalese war, also known as the sino-gorkha war and in chinese as the campaign of gorkha, was a war fought between the qing dynasty of china and the kingdom of nepal in the late 18th century following an invasion of tibet by the nepalese gorkhas.

entries.label: Sino-Portuguese Treaty of Peking
entries.lead: the sino-portuguese treaty of peking was a treaty signed on 1 december 1887 between the kingdom of portugal and the qing dynasty.
terms: tratado de amizade e comercio sino-portugues

entries.label: Sino-Soviet border conflict
entries.lead: the sino-soviet border conflict, also known as the sino-soviet crisis, was a seven-month undeclared military conflict between the soviet union and china in 1969, following the sino-soviet split.

entries.label: Sino-Vietnamese War
entries.lead: the sino-vietnamese war was a war which occurred in early 1979 between china and vietnam.

entries.label: Sioux Wars
entries.lead: the sioux wars were a series of conflicts between the united states and various subgroups of the sioux people which occurred in the later half of the 19th century.

entries.label: Sitawaka campaign
entries.lead: the sitawaka campaign of 1594 was a successful military operation carried out by the portuguese empire and sinhalese forces against the kingdom of sitawaka.

entries.label: Six-Day War
entries.lead: the six-day war, or the 1967 arab–israeli war, was fought between israel and a coalition of arab states, primarily egypt, syria, and jordan, in the context of the arab–israeli conflict.

entries.label: Six Days' Campaign
entries.lead: the six days' campaign was a final series of victories by the forces of napoleon i of france as the sixth coalition closed in on paris.

entries.label: Six Years' War

entries.label: Skanderbeg's Italian expedition
entries.lead: skanderbeg's italian expedition (1460–1462) was undertaken to aid his ally ferdinand i of naples, whose rulership was threatened by the angevin dynasty.

entries.label: Skanderbeg's rebellion
entries.lead: skanderbeg's rebellion was an almost 25-year long anti-ottoman rebellion led by the albanian military commander skanderbeg in what is today albania and north macedonia.

entries.label: Skirmish at Bender
entries.lead: the skirmish at bender was devised to remove charles xii of sweden from the ottoman empire after his military defeats in russia.

entries.label: Skirmish at Cerigo Channel
entries.lead: the skirmish at cerigo channel was a battle between a fleet of the holy league, led by marcantonio colonna in absence of john of austria, and the ottoman armada built after the battle of lepanto, captained by occhiali.

entries.label: Skirmish at Many Branch Point
entries.lead: on 10 june 1982, in the closing days of the falklands war, many branch point, a ridge near port howard in west falkland, was the site of a minor skirmish between the argentine and british armed forces.

entries.label: Skirmish at Top Malo House
entries.lead: the skirmish at top malo house took place on 31 may 1982 during the falklands war between argentine special forces from 602 commando company and the british royal marines of the mountain and arctic warfare cadre (m&awc).

entries.label: Skirmish of Pastrengo (1848)
entries.lead: the skirmish of pastrengo, also known as battle of pastrengo or charge of pastrengo, was fought between the piedmontese and austrian army on 30 april 1848, in the course of the first italian war of independence.

entries.label: Skirmish off Narsapur
entries.lead: the skirmish off narsapur took place on 14 december 1643 at the road off narsapur in golconda between two danish ships and one bengali ship.

entries.label: Skopje fire of 1689
entries.lead: the fire of skopje started on 26 october 1689 and lasted for two days, burning much of the city; only some stone-built structures, such as the fortress and some churches and mosques, were relatively undamaged.

entries.label: Slachter's Nek Rebellion
entries.lead: the slachter's nek rebellion was an uprising against the british colonial government by boers in 1815 on the eastern border of the cape colony.

entries.label: Slaughter of the Knezes
entries.lead: the slaughter of the knezes was a campaign of organized murders and assaults of notable serbs in the belgrade pashalik in january–february 1804 by the renegade janissaries known as "dahije", who had seized power in a coup against the vizier hadji mustafa pasha in 1800–1801.

entries.label: The Slave Trade Act 1807
entries.lead: an act of the united kingdom parliament prohibiting the atlantic slave trade throughout the british empire, in force from 1 may 1807 after eighteen years of failed bills.
terms: abolition of the slave trade act 1807
variants: Abolition of the Slave Trade Act 1807

entries.label: The Slavery Abolition Act 1833
entries.lead: an act of the united kingdom parliament, carried by earl grey’s reforming whig administration, which abolished slavery across the british empire by having the government buy the freedom of the enslaved.

entries.label: Slaying of the Basques
entries.lead: the slaying of the basques was the last documented massacre in icelandic history.

entries.label: Slovak–Hungarian War
entries.lead: the slovak–hungarian war, or little war (hungarian: kis haboru, slovak: mala vojna), was a war fought from 23 march to 31 march 1939 between the first slovak republic and hungary in eastern slovakia.

entries.label: Slovak National Uprising
entries.lead: the slovak national uprising was an attempted insurrection organised by the slovak resistance during the second world war.

entries.label: Slovene peasant revolt of 1515
entries.lead: the slovene peasant revolt, also known as the all-slovene peasant uprising, took place in 1515.

entries.lead: the smolensk war (1632–1634) was fought between the polish–lithuanian commonwealth and russia.

entries.lead: the snake war (1864–1868) was an irregular war fought by the united states of america against the "snake indians," the settlers' term for northern paiute, bannock and western shoshone bands who lived along the snake river.

entries.label: Mário Soares elected president
entries.lead: soares won the second round in february 1986, narrowly, becoming the first civilian head of state in sixty years and completing the return of the military to barracks begun by the revision of 1982.

entries.label: Sơn Tây campaign
entries.lead: the son tay campaign was a campaign fought by the french to capture the strategically important city of son tay in tonkin from liu yongfu's black flag army and allied contingents of vietnamese and chinese troops.

entries.label: Sonderbund War
entries.lead: the sonderbund war of november 1847 was a civil war in switzerland, then still a relatively loose confederacy of cantons.

entries.label: Souliote War (1803)
entries.lead: the war between the souliotes of epirus and the ruler of the autonomous ottoman pashalik of yanina, ali pasha, in 1803, was the last of a series of conflicts, known as the souliote wars, that led to the capitulation and expulsion of the souliotes from their homeland.

entries.label: South African Wars (1879–1915)
entries.lead: the south african wars, including but also known as the confederation wars, were a series of wars that occurred in the southern portion of the african continent between 1879 and 1915.

entries.label: South Lebanon conflict (1985–2000)
entries.lead: the south lebanon conflict was an armed conflict that took place in israeli-occupied southern lebanon from 1982 or 1985 until israel's withdrawal in 2000.

entries.label: South Sudanese Civil War
entries.lead: the south sudanese civil war was a multi-sided civil war in south sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces.

entries.label: Southern Cross Expedition
entries.lead: the southern cross expedition, otherwise known as the british antarctic expedition, 1898–1900, was the first british venture of the heroic age of antarctic exploration, and the forerunner of the more celebrated journeys of robert falcon scott and ernest shackleton.

entries.label: Soviet-Afghan War
entries.lead: the soviet–afghan war took place in afghanistan from december 1979 to february 1989.

entries.label: Soviet invasion of Manchuria
entries.lead: the soviet invasion of manchuria, formally known as the manchurian strategic offensive operation or simply the manchurian operation (russian: маньчжурская операция), began on 8 august 1945 with the soviet union’s invasion of the empire of japan’s puppet states of manchukuo and mengjiang, in japanese

entries.label: Soviet invasion of Poland
entries.lead: the soviet invasion of poland was a military conflict by the soviet union without a formal declaration of war.

entries.label: Soviet–Japanese border conflicts
entries.lead: the soviet–japanese border conflicts were a series of minor and major conflicts fought between the soviet union (led by joseph stalin), mongolia (led by khorloogiin choibalsan) and japan (led by hirohito) in northeast asia from 1932 to 1939.

entries.label: Spain and the American Revolutionary War
entries.lead: spain, through its alliance with france and as part of the anglo-french war (1778–1783) with britain, played an important role in the independence of the united states.
terms: spain and the american revolutionary war

entries.label: The Spanish–American War
entries.lead: fought between 21 april and 13 august 1898, after the uss maine blew up in havana harbour on 15 february and political pressure overcame a president who had not sought a war.

entries.label: Spanish American wars of independence
entries.lead: the spanish american wars of independence were a series of conflicts that took place across the spanish empire during the early 19th century.
terms: guerras de independencia na america espanhola

entries.label: Spanish annexation of the Dominican Republic

terms: spanish annexation of the dominican republic

entries.label: Spanish assault on Djerba (1510)
entries.lead: the spanish assault on djerba was a 1510 military expedition directed by ferdinand ii of aragon against the tunisian island of djerba.

entries.label: Spanish assault on French Florida
entries.lead: the spanish assault on french florida began as part of imperial spain's geopolitical strategy of developing colonies in the new world to protect its claimed territories against incursions by other european powers.

entries.label: Spanish attempts to reconquer Mexico
entries.lead: spanish attempts to reconquer mexico were efforts by the spanish government to regain possession of its former colony of new spain, resulting in episodes of war comprised in clashes between the newly born mexican nation and spain.
